Description: Headquarters: ignitionit.com URL: https://ignitionit.com Fully Remote · Work from home · Full-time (Eastern or Pacific time zones) · Apple-first TL;DR ignitionit.com is a seasoned, Apple-first MSP — in business for almost 30 years — and we're hiring a Help Desk Technician to be the friendly, capable first voice our clients reach when something isn't working. This position is a remote, work-from-home, full-time role. We've written this as a junior-to-mid-level job description because that's where most great people start on our team. But if you're more seasoned — comfortable in identity, MDM, or security work — don't scroll past. We'd be delighted to find someone who can step in higher up the ladder, and we'll happily talk about a more senior scope and comp if that's you. What the actual job??? Unlike many IT shops, we believe that the technology is the tactic. The actual job is making people feel taken care of. One of our core values is “49% tech support, 51% human support.” You'll succeed by configuring devices, resetting access, untangling email, and chasing down the gremlin that's been haunting someone's conference room. But you'll know you succeeded when a client exhales and says, “Thank goodness you're on it!” That Warm Fuzzy Feeling™ is the actual product. The green lights on the dashboard are just how we get there. In a typical week, you might: Onboard a new hire at a fast-growing startup: provision their Mac, set up their Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 accounts, enroll the device in MDM, and make sure day one feels effortless. Offboard a departing employee cleanly — recover the laptop, revoke access, and close the loop so nothing's left dangling. All boxes checked, ticket notated and closed, client followed up with. Field a "my email stopped working" ticket that turns out to be a DNS thing, a phishing-filter thing, or a "they changed their password on their phone three weeks ago" thing. Help a family office or RIA get a touchy Zoom Room or conference-room AV setup behaving before a meeting — over the phone. Triage the queue so phones get answered fast, emails don't rot, and nobody feels forgotten — even when the honest answer is, “We're on it, but here's the realistic timeline." ⠀ You'll be the front line: helping with what you can, researching what you can't, and pinging the rest of the team when you're genuinely stuck. That last part is a skill, not a weakness — knowing when to ask is half the job. About ignitionit.com We're one of the oldest Apple Technical Partners on the planet, and one of the only certified Apple Premier Partners — that’s kinda like getting knighted by the ghost of Steve Jobs. We started where you’d expect to find Macs (creative agencies, non-profits, education) but our primary clients today are cutting-edge, venture-backed AI SaaS startups, VC and private equity firms, registered investment advisors — many of them operating under stringent compliance expectations (SOC 2, SEC). That means we hold ourselves to a higher standard than the scrappy shop we started as. Polished, reliable, security-minded work is the baseline now — but always with a smile! What hasn't changed: relationships are still our most valuable currency — with clients, with vendors, and with each other. We're a tight, supportive team. We teach each other what we know, cover for each other when life throws a punch, and care a little too much about doing things the right way. We're still a bit weird, and our clients seem to like us that way. We move fast, priorities shift, it’s not always documented (whatever it is), our tool set and list of supported platforms is sprawling, and some days the to-do list is longer than you'd like. If you can stay warm under pressure, create order out of chaos, learn new stuff fast because you love it, and speak up when you need help, you'll thrive here. If you need a rigid, fully-documented, never-changes environment where nobody trusts you with admin access, where you will be micro-managed so you never have to wonder whether or not you’re doing the right thing, this isn't it. You’ll have a ton of independence on our team, and freedom to use your best judgment to get the ball over the finish line, but that also means we expect you to be naturally responsible, honest, and highly accountable — to yourself, your teammates, and the clients. As they say, the price of freedom is eternal vigilance. The tech you'll work with (and grow into) Day one, you'll be living in: Apple at the core — macOS, iOS, Apple Business Manager, and MDM (Jamf / Iru / Intune / Workspace ONE / and more) Yes, PCs too — about one-third of our users are driving Windows Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 admin consoles Identity and access — SSO, MFA, and security keys (Okta, Entra ID, Yubikey, and friends) Lots of other security tools — our stack is constantly evolving and may vary from client to client The everyday productivity stack — Slack, Zoom, conference-room AV, networking basics (Meraki), and endpoint tooling ⠀ You don't need to know all of this. You need to be the kind of person who wants to. As you grow, there's a clear path into infrastructure administration, project architecture and implementation, and — for the right person — security and compliance work (phishing simulations, endpoint detection, SOC 2 / CIS / SEC readiness, due diligence questionnaire support, etc.). That's where our most senior people live, and it's wide open. Who we hope you are The hard requirements — we won't move forward unless you: Can work standard business hours in Eastern or Pacific time zones (we currently need both) Have a quiet home workspace and reliable broadband Have proven Apple aptitude — you actually use and like the Apple ecosystem Have at least 5 years of IT support experience on the job. ⠀ Everything else — and this is the longer list, on purpose. We figure technical skills are teachable; character takes a lot longer. So we're looking for someone who: Genuinely cares — about clients, teammates, and doing right by people Loves to learn, and proves it in how they spend their time Reads, and writes clearly — clear writing is clear thinking, and you'll do a lot of it Stays calm and kind with a frustrated person on the other end of the line Can tell the difference between good customer service and fantastic customer service, and refuses to settle for the former Notices when something's being done inefficiently and fixes it (you may boast about it later, that’s fine) Proofreads their own work (yes, we noticed whether you proofread your application) Has a sense of humor, and doesn't take themselves too seriously Regarding AI Our company founder/CEO is headquartered in the Bay Area. We work with innovative, ambitious companies developing AI products. Our team members hold a range of opinions about whether AI is “good or bad” for humans, but at the end of the day, we embrace the plain fact that it is here, we must embrace it to evolve, and our clients increasingly depend on us to help them embrace it, too, to help them evolve and stay competitive. Our CEO's opinion: AI will not replace human labor any time soon; rather, AI is a new opportunity to either (a) get things done faster, or (b) get a much higher quality of output than before. If you’re an AI tinkerer, great! We want to hear how you’re using it and see your latest vibe project. If you’re allergic to AI or have no interest in learning new habits to work effectively with it, this is not the place for you. Compensation & logistics Base salary: Applicants outside the USA will be compensated according to your local employment market. For applicants closer to the junior side who are located in the USA, $50,000–$65,000/yr, depending on experience level and your local geographical price index. With experience, comp goes up from there. Genuinely experienced, more senior candidates can be slotted higher — let's talk. Type & location: Full-time, work from home, fully remote. Eastern or Pacific time zones. Benefits: Medical / dental / vision for the employee, 401(k) with employer contribution, 2 weeks of PTO annually to start, and a stipend for your home internet. How to apply The first step is really easy and only takes 10 minutes — no resume, no cover letter, no essays. Here's how: Take this online Culture Index assessment (about 10 minutes): We use it to screen for people whose natural wiring fits how our team works. If your profile lines up with what we're looking for, we'll reach out and ask you to complete a 60-minute TestGorilla assessment for critical thinking skills, send us your resume, and maybe a couple of other items. From there, we conduct between 2-4 video interviews. One of these might be a live technical assessment. If the Culture Index step feels like a strange way to start a job application — that's kind of the point. Remember the phrase Think Different? Ignition is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and will consider all qualified applicants. Good luck in your search — and may the Force be with you! of Expel's detection coverage across the whole Microsoft security estate Put Microsoft telemetry from across our customer base in front of you — a breadth of real-world environments no single catching drift before it costs us efficacy Tell us where Microsoft's native detections are strong enough to lean on, where they're noisy or shallow, and where Expel needs its own layer Make SOC analysts faster by automating Microsoft-specific investigative workflows against the Graph, Defender, Sentinel, and Entra APIs Partner with Engineering on our Microsoft integrations — ingestion, API limits and throttling, and schema mapping Answer the hard questions from the SOC, CS, and Sales — and mentor the people asking them Help customers understand what they're actually covered for, what You’ll work closely with and report to our Senior AI & Design Lead to turn product requirements into robust, secure, and well-documented applications, as well as maintain existing ones. Architect reliable, performant backends and APIs; familiarity with AWS (Lambda, ECS/Fargate, API Gateway, RDS/DynamoDB, S3, CloudFront, Cognito, etc.) is important. Solid understanding of web security best practices (OWASP, secure storage, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets management). Experience building systems in or adjacent to healthcare, education, or compliance-heavy environments is a plus. Excellent async communication, code ownership, and ability to work with a small, senior-led team. Comfort working from a clear product brief and also proposing improvements proactively. Familiarity with logging, monitoring, and observability tools. Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process) Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare: Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n. Stack Next.js (App Router) Clerk for authentication Convex for data + backend logic n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation TypeScript Requirements Public page The fictional company name is LendLoop . Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.” Show: A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex. A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk. Authenticated experience Only signed-in users can: List a tool with: name category (power tools, garden, kitchen, camping, etc.) condition short description Request to borrow a tool for a date range. Approve or decline requests on their own tools. Mark a loan as returned. Show: All tools with availability status, filterable by category. “My listings”, “My requests”, and “Incoming requests” views. Nice, minimal layout. Roles & rules Have two roles: admin : Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”. user : Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing. Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI. Automation with n8n Build at least two n8n workflows: Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs. Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex. Secure the integration in both directions: Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side. Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON. Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders. Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently. (Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”. Deliverables A GitHub repository with the app source code. Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository. A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions. A short note on what you would change to run this in production. Description: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable. Our stack is Python ( FastAPI ) on AWS , with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows. Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD . What You Will Do: Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end. Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails. Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production. Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality. Drive the full software development lifecycle , translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans. What We Are Looking For: 5+ years building and operating production backend systems , with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end. Deep fluency in your primary backend language , and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python ; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly. Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one. Sound reasoning under ambiguity : you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change. Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations , including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar). Professional written English , enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs. Even Better: AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience. Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions. A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal. How We Hire: We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build: 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit.. 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review. You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment. What We Offer: Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package. Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work. The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI , tackling hard problems with high ownership. A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement. If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk! Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: About CoLab At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner. We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster. Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+. About the Role Modern engineering teams invest a significant amount of time and money on simulation. Before anything gets built, teams need confidence that a design is going to work: structurally, thermally, aerodynamically, etc. Simulation is one of the main ways they build that confidence. But the way teams share and review simulation results to make decisions is still pretty broken. Engineers are exporting videos, taking screenshots, dropping them into PowerPoint, and then trying to make decisions through email threads, meetings, or disconnected slide decks. The actual decision-making ends up separated from the underlying simulation data, which means context gets lost, feedback is hard to trace, and important engineering knowledge disappears into the workflow. CoLab already helps engineering teams review CAD, capture feedback, and make better design decisions in one connected workspace. Now we’re extending that same idea into simulation. The goal is simple: make simulation results collaborative, reviewable, and traceable in the same way CoLab does for CAD today. We’re starting a new product team focused on bringing simulation review into CoLab. As one of the first engineers on that team, you’ll help define how simulation data gets ingested, visualized, discussed, and connected back to real engineering decisions. There are a lot of interesting technical problems here: large datasets, high-performance visualization, viewer interactions, data pipelines, and user experiences that need to work for mechanical engineers doing critical product development work. The first phase is about learning the product, the customers, and the review workflows we already support today. You’ll spend time embedded with our Engineering Reviews team, learning how engineers collaborate in CoLab, where the current product is strong, and where simulation creates a new set of problems we need to solve. From there, you’ll help build the foundation for a new Simulation team - not just technically, but from a product perspective as well. We want to build something customers actually need and will use in their day-to-day work, and that requires a highly product oriented approach. Our Ideal Candidate You're the kind of developer who wants to understand why a feature matters before deciding how to build it. You enjoy owning complex technical problems, but you also enjoy talking with product managers, designers, and customers to understand what success actually looks like. You make thoughtful technical decisions independently and know when to bring others into the conversation. Experience working with simulation software is a significant advantage. Maybe you've worked with FEA, CFD, multiphysics simulations, scientific visualization, or engineering data platforms. You understand the kinds of problems engineers are trying to solve. This is a good fit for someone who likes ambiguity, wants to work closely with our product and leadership teams, and cares about the connection between technical decisions and customer value. You’ll have a meaningful role in shaping both the architecture and the user experience for a new capability that we think can become a major part of engineering review in CoLab. What You'll Do Help design and build CoLab's next-generation simulation review capabilities. Build services that ingest and process simulation data from industry-standard engineering software. Develop high-performance visualization experiences capable of displaying large simulation datasets. Partner closely with Product, Design, and customers to validate ideas before building them. Spend time embedded with the Engineering Reviews team to develop deep product and customer understanding before transitioning onto the Simulation team. Contribute to architectural decisions that will shape this product area for years to come. Improve performance, scalability, and reliability as simulation capabilities grow. Collaborate with engineers across the platform to ensure simulation becomes a seamless part of the broader CoLab experience. Qualifications We're looking for someone with: 8+ years building production software in a modern engineering environment. Strong experience designing scalable backend systems and customer-facing applications. Experience building complex data visualization or graphics-intensive applications. The ability to work independently while collaborating closely with teammates. A product mindset - you think about customer outcomes as much as technical implementation. Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex ideas clearly. Experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA), CFD, or other CAE workflows. Experience with engineering simulation platforms Experience with CAD, PLM, or engineering software development. Large engineering datasets and high-performance rendering. The Extra Details Full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package, including stock options. Extended health benefits, unlimited paid vacation, and RRSP/401K matching. Remote-first across North America Equity Note Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification - your potential is what matters most to us. Originally posted on Himalayas

Fluency with modern AI development tools and coding agents, paired with the discipline to verify, test, and own everything you ship. Stack-agnostic adaptability, so you pick up new languages and frameworks quickly. (Our stack today is Elixir and Phoenix; prior experience is welcome but not required.) A strong foundation in software design, architecture, and the practices that keep systems reliable, including testing, continuous integration, code review, and containerization. Clear, direct communication, so you can express intent precisely to both teammates and the tools you work with. The instincts of a senior engineer: you lead projects, mentor others, and raise the level of the people around you. A drive to keep learning and to help shape how the team builds. Why you'll love it here Join a progressive team that lives on the forefront of technology, where innovation and curiosity are the norm. We invest seriously in modern tooling, including the best AI tools, and we’re always looking for the next approach that makes the team better. Competitive salary, benefits, and an environment where work-life balance is more than just a catchphrase. You’ll play a crucial role in a platform that enterprises rely on to manage their IT, working alongside a talented and motivated team. Make your voice heard AHEAD recognizes the value of diverse perspectives. In our ever-evolving tech landscape, the insights you bring from your own journey can reshape our collective experience. If you’ve had experiences, both good and challenging, with other platforms, technologies, or ways of working, they’ll become an asset here. The Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN) is the branch of the United States Food and Drug Administration that regulates food, dietary supplements, cosmetics, drugs, biologics, medical devices, and radiological products. The FDA expects between 2-5 new applications/systems to be added to the BPA per year over the duration of this contract. CFSAN will issue individual Task Orders for the Contractor to provide IT Lifecycle Support for the CFSAN IT portfolio of systems as needed. Representative tasks to be performed. If an FDA template does not exist, the Contractor may be tasked with drafting a template for approval by the COR. Task 2: O&M and DME Architecture Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the full range of architecture support services in order to formulate the integrated, end-to-end automated systems that provide enhanced IT capabilities necessary to support CFSAN business and mission processes. The goal is a stable evolutionary progression from an organization’s current state to its envisioned future state by identifying tools and technologies that work together to satisfy the needs or changing business needs of the CFSAN users. Task 3: Development, Modernization, and Major Enhancement: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of system development lifecycle support services necessary to develop and enhance CFSAN IT systems and tools as well as their external interfaces to FDA Enterprise and Center Systems and applications. Tasks may encompass the complete lifecycle of activities required for database, application and tool development including, but not limited to requirements elicitation, analysis and validation; system design; code generation; testing; deployment; and documentation. The Contractor shall also develop, support and evolve designs, customizations and process automation such as interfaces, templates, scripts, workflows, interfaces to permit reviewer access to analytics/tools, and reports. Deliverable products shall be validated and tested to ensure that they meet applicable/specified standards, policy, business requirements. Task 4: Systems Integration and Engineering Services: The Contractor shall support CFSAN with integration services. The Contractor shall focus on the development and deployment of integrated information systems that reflect the introduction of a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) orientation and, moreover, places an emphasis on the recommended acquisition and re-use of existing components—be they FDA components, HHS components, or components acquired from any other source. Task 5: Data Migration and Management Support: The Contractor shall provide data management support for activities related to the development and execution of data architectures, data policies, practices, and procedures that properly manage the full data lifecycle needs of CFSAN. Task #6 - Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services Task 6: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of operations and maintenance support services necessary to maintain CFSAN IT systems. The Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the “lights on” availability, reliability, and security of the CFSAN IT portfolio through the full range of O&M services. The Contractor shall maintain, support, and evolve code, scripts, views, triggers, jobs, designs, documentation, reports, and templates. The Contractor shall analyze and report on the impact of infrastructure, software upgrades, capacity, and all changes to the technical environment. These day-to-day operations, maintenance, and help desk support ensures that the systems perform their intended functions. Task 7: System and Data Disposition: The Contractor shall identify, recommend and implement the retirement and consolidation of systems, components, technologies, tools and data when they meet the appropriate disposition stage of the lifecycle as defined in the EPLC. Task 8: Training Support for O&M and DME: The Contractor shall provide training services to CFSAN stakeholders for existing applications, application changes, or newly developed applications. The Contractor shall assess the level of capability of the users and the need for training. The Contractor shall prepare a training plan, the training materials, and arrange and conduct training sessions. The training plan and materials shall be provided to the COR for review and approval prior to training. Task 9: Transition Activities: The Contractor shall provide the transition-in and transition-out of activities to develop, operate, and manage the CFSAN IT portfolio. It is the responsibility of both the incoming Contractor and outgoing Contractor to ensure a smooth transition, with minimal disruption to services and support for users. The purpose of the transition is to transfer expert knowledge, data, and artifacts that are used to support applications from the incumbent Contractor to the successor Contractor efficiently. *** Enterprise Performance Lifecycle (EPLC) Agile Methodology: The Food and Drug Administration maintains a project management methodology framework that incorporates best government and commercial practices through a consistent and repeatable process, and provides a standard structure for planning, managing and overseeing IT projects over their entire life cycle. Description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing. We are hiring a Junior developer with a proven track record in Python and/or Go. As part of the Observability team, you will develop a cloud-native monitoring stack that composes best-in-class open-source monitoring tools. The stack is opinionated, resilient, and scalable, providing deep insights out of the box. The user experience is polished and seamless for the end-users, and its administrators will enjoy smooth, lightweight Day 1 and Day 2 operations. This is an exciting opportunity for a software engineer passionate about open source software, Linux, Kubernetes, and Observability. Build a rewarding, meaningful career working with the best and brightest people in technology at Canonical , the growing international software company behind Ubuntu. The monitoring stack will monitor applications running on a mix of cloud technologies such as Kubernetes and OpenStack, as well as bare-metal, virtual machines and containers. The stack will be capable of monitoring applications and infrastructure irrespective of whether they are operated by Juju, and will leverage multiple data sources at various levels of the architecture, including Juju itself, to contextualize the collected telemetry and insights delivered to the end-users. You can read more about the project here and here. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Description: Software Engineer (Remote) Are you a software engineer starting your career who would like to help us to scale the next generation of AI-powered experiences for thousands of companies and hundreds of millions of shopper sessions? Who we are We are an exciting new startup, Product Genius , bringing the power of cutting-edge AI to small and medium-sized businesses so that they can compete online. Our AI-powered mobile shopping experience solves the problem that shopping is still difficult on a mobile phone even though 70% of web traffic is on mobile, 70% of checkouts happen on desktop. We have proven in A/B tests that our product ( Product Genius ) removes the friction of shopping on mobile, bringing mobile conversion to desktop rates. Stores can sign up for our Product Genius through a 1-click install. We know we are onto something, and now we need to work on scaling as we continue to incorporate our learnings from our initial batches of customers into our offering. Our lead investor and board member has over two decades of experience in eCommerce, having co-founded and built two >$billion startups, Endeca and Toast, and having funded many other successful eCommerce startups. Our CEO has over two decades of experience building startup products with deep learning-based technology. Much of our team is located in Boston, Philadelphia, and Chicago. We work together collaboratively over Slack and Zoom, getting together periodically in person. Who you are Your motivation is to make the experience awesome for the end users. Knowing that your work had a real impact for real-world customers makes you super happy. You love checking stuff off a to-do list, but also appreciate being on a fast-moving team where our to-do list continues to evolve. You love creating beautiful code and refactoring messy code, you get an intrinsic thrill from it. That said, you understand the need of a startup to sometimes deliver functionality to the end user with code that isn't super pretty, at least at first. You are generous with others and collaborate well in a team environment. You are a great team player who enjoys pair-coding with other engineers and researchers. You have a strong interest in being part of a successful high-growth company, and part of a team building AI-first software products. You are proficient in backend software engineering and technologies such as server side Python 3.x, caching, reinforcement learning and/or machine learning architectures, modern database technologies, and cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP A working knowledge of front-end technologies such as HTML5, React, Node.js, Websockets, etc. is a big plus. Ask for help when you need it, make progress when you dont, and learn how to tell the difference. Work in an agile environment, rapidly delivering shippable features into production. Learn to understand and empathize with our customers who are awesome entrepreneurs growing small and medium sized businesses in their communities. We provide comprehensive healthcare (including dental and vision), remote workspace cash benefit, 401k plan, and stock options. You may not feel that you have all of the experience and skills listed above, but if you are very excited about this role, please apply anyway. We have found that people who are passionate to join us are also often the people who we are passionate to hire. We value a diverse team, and we have seen firsthand that as our team diversity has increased, so has the quality of our ideas, teamwork, and delivery. Description: At In Tandem , we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions. As a Staff+ Builder , you're on the frontier of continuously redefining how we deliver software and exercise judgement in a constantly evolving landscape — a true AI-native builder expanding products and how they get built. Some of the best work here starts with no brief, no team and no playbook. We want someone who sees that as the appeal: who takes an idea from zero to one and cares personally whether it gets traction. This role exists to bring that way of working into In Tandem , wherever the organization needs it most. This is an evergreen role. We will shape the specific team and scope with you as we learn where your strengths meet the most important opportunities across our products and platform. As we move through conversations, we will discuss the concrete problem area, collaborators, and expectations for the opening we are considering together. What you will do: Seek out problems worth building for. Talk with users, learn from support and product data, and pay attention to changes in our markets. Turn those signals into a clear view of what matters, then take initiative inside shared priorities, and bring partners along as you learn. Take it from zero to one. Start where there is no structure. Get a first version in front of real users quickly, find out whether anyone cares, and do the unglamorous work that earns early traction. Own the outcome, not just the code. Carry useful work into production. Shape a focused first version, build it, and learn from real use. Define how you will judge success before you build, then use the evidence to improve, expand, or stop the work. Raise the pace and quality of engineering. Identify places where an AI-enabled workflow can shorten the path from idea to shipped software. Build the tools, context, checks, and feedback loops that let other engineers use it with confidence. Own the hard decisions. Move work forward when requirements are incomplete, make your reasoning visible, and bring consequential tradeoffs to the right partners. Choose when to prototype, when to invest in durable architecture, and how to verify that a system is correct, safe, and useful. Connect the pieces. Work across product and engineering boundaries. Bring depth in a core platform and enough range across APIs, web, mobile, and infrastructure to help a feature succeed end to end. Make others stronger. Share working examples, explain tradeoffs clearly, invite criticism, and help teams adopt what proves effective. What strong work could look like: The shape of the work will depend on the team. Examples include: Recognizing a recurring difficulty in a family workflow, validating it with users and partners, and shipping a focused improvement across client and service boundaries. Launching something small with no existing team or process, getting it to its first real users, and iterating on their feedback until it was adopted or you chose to stop. Turning a promising agent prototype into a reliable engineering workflow with evaluation, tests, observability, and clear human review points. Removing a recurring bottleneck in delivery so teams can make more high-quality changes with less coordination. Connecting an emerging user or market need to our product strategy, testing the opportunity with a small build, and using the result to decide whether it deserves more investment. These are examples of the work this role might own, not claims that those projects are planned or assigned. What you bring: What you bring Staff-level impact as a hands-on engineer: you have shaped technical direction, built important systems, and helped other people deliver stronger work. An owner's mindset. You've started something with little structure, such as a product, feature, internal tool, open-source project or company. You know how to test a premise with a prototype and how to recognize when a prototype needs stronger engineering before it can be trusted in production. Product judgment and curiosity about users and markets. You can explain why a problem mattered, how you chose it with others, and what changed for users or the business because of what you built. Strong judgment about architecture, quality, security, and user experience. You know which decisions need close attention and which can be accelerated. Depth in at least one engineering area, with the curiosity and fundamentals to work effectively across the stack. Low ego, high integrity, and a habit of making your reasoning visible so others can learn from and improve it. What will stand out Show us a piece of work you helped take from an uncertain opportunity to a useful result. If it started from zero, tell us what you did to get the first users and what you did when nobody was available to help. What user or market signal made the problem worth pursuing? Description: ​ Job Description - Senior Software Engineer Reports To - Engineering Manager Summary AxisCare is hiring a full-time, fully remote Senior Software Engineer to help us build, ship, and maintain the market-leading SaaS platform powering the home care industry, and to help us reimagine how software gets made in the age of AI. We're no longer building the car by hand, so to speak. We're building the factory that makes great cars, with humans in the loop where the human touch matters most. (Read more about how we think AI is changing product development.) We're looking for engineers who've already internalized this shift. Engineers who push AI tools to their breaking point, then push again three months later when the models improve. Engineers who move from idea to working software in hours instead of weeks, and who bring the judgment to know when the output is actually good. There will always be a need for people who deeply understand our customers' most important problems, solve them with high-quality software, and run that software reliably in production. That's the work that endures, and that's the work we're hiring for. What You'll Do Collaborate with product leaders to spike on possibilities and prototype aggressively, often putting working software in front of stakeholders before the old process would have finished a PRD, then quickly iterate from there. Mentor junior and mid-level engineers in code design, systems thinking, and driving AI agents effectively: when to trust output, when to throw it out, and how to maintain code quality when the machine is doing the typing. Write backend business logic, extend our API, integrate with third-party services, build frontend UI, and tackle issues throughout the codebase. All using AI fluently as a force multiplier, not a crutch. Improve system performance and resilience, upgrade our tech stack, and go after the pipe dreams that used to be too expensive to try. Own what you ship in production. Home care agencies rely on our software to run their business every day, so we instrument, observe, and debug what we build. We treat reliability as a first-class feature, not an afterthought. What We're Looking For A product-minded engineer who deeply interrogates user problems before jumping to solutions. AI makes it dangerously easy to build the wrong thing quickly. A systems thinker who looks beyond the element at hand to the broader system and the dynamics at play within it. An AI power user with substance. You've moved past "I tried Cursor once." You drive agents to carry out real intent on real codebases, have opinions about where today's models break down drawn from real experience, and have habits for catching those failures before they ship. A quality-conscious builder. High-quality software is both valuable to the business now and easy to change later. AI lets us change software quickly, which makes the "easy to change later" part more important than ever. A strong writer. Remote work demands it, clear writing is clear thinking, and clear thinking is how you get the biggest impact from AI. A team lead for 1–2 engineers, but also fully capable of taking substantial features from concept to completion solo. Experience required: 5+ years as a professional software engineer on teams building full stack cloud-native web apps. Ideally with PHP, but any object-oriented language works too. React apps in TypeScript Experience building well-structured, readily comprehensible, easily maintainable software that balances practicality with elegance MySQL, using both PHP-based ORMs and raw SQL Designing and building RESTful APIs, and integrating with third-party APIs Able to work remotely from the Eastern, Central, or Mountain time zones Qualified to work in the United States or Canada What We'd Be Excited to Find Experience building HIPAA-compliant software Experience with EMR/EHR systems used in clinical care Concrete examples of AI-enabled workflows you've built that meaningfully changed how your team ships. Custom agents, evals, prompt libraries, internal tooling, etc. Working Conditions Manual dexterity required to use desktop computer and peripherals Compensation and Equipment Salary (TBD based on job experience and skill level) Medical insurance is covered in full for the employee (Medical, Dental and Vision) Company will provide laptop and other needed computer equipment How to Apply Apply with a brief resume and either a written or video cover letter. We review the cover letter before anything else in your application, so this really matters. This is your single biggest opportunity to improve your chances, and video submissions go right to the front of the line. Prompt: Tell us about something you're proud to have built. Tell us how AI has changed the way you work in the last six to twelve months with specific examples. Tell us why this position is the one you've been hoping to find. Written: No more than 600 words. We're looking for clarity of thought and strong communication. Use AI if you want, but don't send slop. Video: 1–2 minutes, linked in the "Website, Blog, or Portfolio" section of your application. Doesn't need to be highly produced. We care about how you think and communicate. We strongly encourage candidates from all backgrounds and every walk of life to apply. Every person on our team brings their own unique perspective, and it’s what makes our products better and our work more rewarding. We’re eager to support you so that you can ship work you’re proud of. Candidates only. No recruiters, please. Our product is a web-based management platform that helps agencies manage CRM and marketing, Caregiver/Client scheduling, billing, payroll and much more. Headquartered in Waco, TX, AxisCare has clients in all 50 states as well as 6 other countries. Description: Software Engineering Intern Are you currently a college student looking to start your career in software engineering? Do you want hands-on experience working with real production systems while learning from experienced engineers? Nucleus Security is seeking a Software Engineering Intern with an interest in full stack development to join our Engineering organization. Location AUS Remote Department Engineering Employment Type Internship (Paid) Due to business and regulatory requirements, we are only able to hire Australian citizens at this time. About Nucleus Security Nucleus Security helps organizations manage and prioritize vulnerabilities at scale by unifying data from scanners, cloud platforms, and other security tools. Our platform ingests, normalizes, and acts on large volumes of security data to help customers improve their security posture efficiently. Role Overview As a Software Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers to contribute to systems that support integrations, workflows, APIs, and internal tooling across the Nucleus platform. This internship is designed for students who are still in college and intend to begin their careers in software engineering. You will contribute to real code used by production systems while working on carefully scoped projects that prioritize learning, code quality, and maintainability. No prior professional software engineering experience is required. What You’ll Work On Depending on team needs and your interests, you may: Leverage AI to build new features and fix bugs in a Cyber Security Vulnerability Management Platform Build out new components for our ReactJS frontend. Work with third party REST APIs to build new ETL integrations. Write and improve automated tests to increase reliability and confidence. Debug issues and learn how to diagnose problems in distributed systems. Collaborate in code reviews and technical discussions with your team. Required Qualifications Have previous internship, co-op, or equivalent experience in software engineering or a related field. Be currently enrolled in a college or university program with plans to graduate on or before June 2027. Be pursuing a degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related field. Be interested in starting a career in software engineering. Be willing to learn, ask questions, and receive feedback. Due to business and regulatory requirements, we are only able to hire Australian citizens at this time. Nice to Have (Not Required) Experience with PHP and modern PHP practices. Experience with Python and modern Python practices. Experience with React and Typescript. Experience with relational databases such as MySQL. Familiarity with REST APIs, JSON, and HTTP. Experience writing or debugging unit tests. Basic familiarity with Git, Linux, or CI/CD concepts. Experience working in an Agile development environment. Interest in cybersecurity, integrations, or developer tooling. Internship Experience & Outcomes Throughout the internship, you will work on one or more well-scoped projects under the guidance of a mentor. At the conclusion of the internship, you will present to the engineering team what you worked on, the problems you tackled, and what you learned. Why Nucleus? At Nucleus Security , you will: Gain hands-on experience working on real-world software systems. Learn professional engineering practices in a supportive, mentorship-driven environment. Collaborate with a high-performing, distributed engineering team. Work remotely with flexibility and a strong emphasis on learning and growth. Nucleus Security is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability. Description: About Abridge Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients. Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems. We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh. The Role We're looking for Software Engineering Interns to join Abridge's Engineering team for a 3-month internship program in Spring 2027, with the possibility of extension. You'll collaborate with our engineering team to build and ship real-world features that translate cutting-edge language model capabilities into dependable clinical systems. With mentorship and guidance, you'll gain hands-on experience designing, coding, and releasing AI-powered software that makes a meaningful impact on clinicians' workflows. What You'll Do Design and build end-to-end features, enhancing our existing systems and contributing to agentic LLM workflows (retrieval pipelines, structured tool use, chained LLM calls) Fix user-facing bugs and issues, and make quality-of-life improvements across our backend and frontend systems Get hands-on with evaluation frameworks that measure accuracy, robustness, and clinical reliability Help prototype with new models, prompting techniques, and open-source orchestration tools (LangChain, LlamaIndex, etc.) Develop a strong user-centric mindset, building empathy for Abridge's clinicians and the challenges they face Collaborate across cross-functional product teams — design, product, machine learning, and infrastructure — to ship features to our customers Receive guidance from an experienced software engineering mentor, and collaborate one-on-one with teammates within your pod What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field A strong interest in pursuing a full-time software engineering role in 2027 — high-performing interns are eligible to receive a return offer AI tooling is already part of how you work — you use it to write, debug, and learn faster, and you know when to trust it vs. verify Passion for and understanding of Abridge's mission A curious, adaptable, and proactive mindset, with a desire to learn and grow in a fast-paced startup environment A collaborative, low-ego mindset — we move fast, and we need team players who are eager to contribute wherever needed Base Salary: $40/hr Must be willing to work from our San Francisco (Potrero) office 5x per week. Description: About Upsun Upsun is the software factory for AI-human workflows. We build the tools that let engineering teams work with confidence, with AI agents and humans working together from the first idea all the way to production. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to move faster without losing control. Upsun brings this together through two products: one that shapes the work, and one that runs it. Upsun Dispatch™: where your team and AI agents work together. Upsun Dispatch keeps the right humans in the loop at the right moments, with human approval built in, full visibility into what’s happening, and no surprises on the bill. Agents do the volume and your team holds the line. Upsun Cloud: where that software runs. Upsun Cloud handles building, deploying, and scaling what your team ships, with: Predictable performance, even at scale Secure, compliant environments by default Real-time observability and cost transparency Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds The name says it all. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation. What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work. Our values: 🌿 We make a positive impact. ✨ We aim for the stars. 💚 We care for each other. Impact of a Software Engineer At Upsun, we build tools that shape how developers create, deploy, and run software. That can mean making an entire application environment available for testing or bringing AI agents and developers together in structured workflows. These challenges require thoughtful engineering: making powerful capabilities easy to use while giving teams control over how their software is built and operated. Our engineering work connects new possibilities with the demands of established systems. It takes curiosity to investigate beyond the obvious answer, technical judgment to weigh different approaches, and the drive to turn ideas into working software. Across technical backgrounds and time zones, we share expertise, question assumptions, and learn from one another to make decisions and move forward. There’s room for different strengths and perspectives to shape what we build next. What to expect End-to-end ownership: Design, build, and maintain software within your team’s area, working with teammates from implementation through release and production support. Technical decisions: Bring your reasoning to design discussions, consider alternative approaches, and help the team move forward with sound trade-offs between delivery, maintainability, and risk. Cross-functional collaboration: Work through interfaces, APIs, and user experience with Engineering, Product, Design, and Support, drawing on the expertise each team brings. AI-assisted engineering: Use AI tools to support development and share approaches that improve how the team works. Quality, security, and reliability: Build these considerations into your work from the outset, including the observability needed to understand its behaviour in production. Shared engineering practice: Exchange knowledge through pairing, code reviews, team sessions, and feedback. Write documentation that gives colleagues the context to understand and build on your work. What you bring Production experience: A track record of delivering reliable production software, with strong programming fundamentals and proficiency in Python, Go, or TypeScript. Depending on the team, your specific language experience might align best with a particular role, but we value the ability to learn new languages and technologies as needs evolve. Systems understanding: The ability to reason about how your work fits into a larger system, including dependencies, data flow, and component failures. APIs and data: Experience building or consuming APIs and working with data stores such as relational databases. Testing and correctness: A habit of writing automated tests, including failure paths, with attention to the consequences of errors for users. Security: An understanding of security best practices in software development. CI/CD practices: Familiarity with cloud environments and CI/CD pipelines. Curiosity and persistence: A drive to understand difficult problems, learn from setbacks, and work with others to find a way forward. AI collaboration : Comfort working with AI as both a tool and a teammate, knowing when to delegate, how to review its output, and taking over when needed. Bonus A background in cloud platforms or developer tools. Experience in areas such as identity and access management, billing, provisioning and orchestration, or frontend development for technical products. Integrating complex third-party services with constraints on contracts, rate limits, and availability. Designing highly available systems. Contributions to developer experience improvements. Where we hire At Upsun, remote work isn’t just a trend: it’s our foundation. Upsunners are a global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We are committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans the globe and the experience spectrum Our team spans more than 30 countries, living the full multicultural experience, and we are currently hiring for this role in Canada, France, Germany, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Although we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries. How we hire Our interview process is a chance for us to understand how you think, what you’ve built, and what you want to take on next, and for you to get to know us. Together, we’ll explore where your strengths and interests meet the challenges our teams are solving. We know a great hire won’t meet every requirement above. If you can see yourself making the team better, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here if someone hadn’t taken a chance on us. You can expect interviews on Google Meet to follow the order below. 45 Minutes with Talent Acquisition 60 Minutes with Hiring Manager 60 Minutes with Team (pair programming session in CoderPad) Depending on the scope of the role, the process may also include: 60 Minutes with Team: Technical deep dive (system design challenge in CoderPad) 45 Minutes with Executive All roles require background checks. What we offer 💡 A product you can believe in - Join us in transforming how businesses build and manage web applications, driven making a positive impact as a proud B Corp . 🏆 An Award-Winning Workplace - We’ve been recognized by Forbes’ Top 30 Companies for Remote Jobs and France’s Best Workplaces for Women. 🗣️ A culture that values your voice - Join a flexible, open, and inclusive work environment where your voice is encouraged, and your ideas shape our growth and evolution. 🌎 A global team - Collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds across the world, embracing different perspectives 🎉 Benefits and perks - Make the most of what matters to you 🏝 Flexible PTO 🩺 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (UK, Canada, France, Spain, USA) 📈 Company stock options 🧠 Professional development budget 💻 Office equipment budget 💆‍♀️ Wellness budget 🧳 Annual team gatherings 🛜 Internet reimbursement 👶 Inclusive parental leave ✈️ Remote work travel program You belong here At Upsun, we celebrate diversity in all its forms and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and supportive workplace where everyone can thrive. We embrace and value different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences, because they make us stronger as a team. Whoever you are, wherever you're from, and whatever path you've taken, you are welcome here. We encourage you to bring your whole self to work, connect with others, and share your passion. If you need accommodations at any stage of our hiring process, please let us know. We're here to ensure an accessible and comfortable experience for you. Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: Join our mission to provide governments with exceptional experiences so they can do the same for their communities! What do we do?💥 We empower governments to deliver exceptional citizen experiences. Check out our ‘About Us’ page for a deep dive into our product and what makes us exceptional. About Clariti Clariti builds community development software for cities and counties: permitting, licensing, plan review, and the workflows that let local governments serve their residents. We are in the middle of an AI-native transformation: AI is becoming part of our products and part of how our engineering pods build them. About the role Clariti 's products run the permitting and community development operations of cities across North America. We are rethinking how that software should work when AI is part of the product and part of how the product gets built, and the engineering pod you would join is at the center of that work. You will join a product engineering pod as a developer. The pod is small and senior, and works inside our Agentic SDLC framework: agent specs, orchestration workflows, reusable prompts, and eval harnesses that let a handful of engineers deliver at multiples of traditional velocity. You will not be typing every line yourself. You will be directing, reviewing, and shaping the work of coding agents, then owning the result as if you had written it, because you are accountable for it either way. This is a product engineering role. Your job is to ship products: features cities will use to issue permits, run inspections, and serve residents, delivered to the quality bar government software demands. What you will do Ship product. Take features from spec through delivery in production, working within the pod's agentic workflow. Own the outcome end to end: correctness, performance, security, and the experience of the person at the counter who has to use it. Work agent-first. Write clear specs and acceptance criteria, direct coding agents to implement them, review the output critically, and iterate. Your leverage is judgment, not keystrokes. Hold the quality bar. Government software is scrutinized differently than consumer software. You test what agents produce, you understand what you ship, and you do not merge what you cannot explain. Improve how the pod works. Feed what you learn about the framework, the workflows, and the agents back to the pod and to the Applied AI team that owns the framework. Velocity is a shared asset; you help keep it high. Learn the domain. Permitting, licensing, plan review, inspections, and the rules cities live under. The best engineers here understand why a workflow exists before they change it. What you bring 7+ years as a software developer shipping production web applications, with deep fundamentals in API design, data modeling, testing, and cloud infrastructure. Real experience building with coding agents and AI-assisted development tools, and a clear-eyed view of what they are good at and where they fail. You have shipped production code this way, not just experimented. Strong written communication. In an agent-first pod, the quality of your specs determines the quality of the code. The habit of reading and understanding what you ship, including code you did not type. You verify; you do not assume. Comfort with pace and ambiguity. The roadmap is ambitious and the pod moves quickly. Nice to have Experience in government, civic, or other regulated software, where auditability and accessibility are requirements rather than preferences. Experience with permitting, land management, or community development systems, or with the operations of a municipal government. Experience with eval-driven development or building evaluation harnesses for AI-generated code. How success is measured 90 days: you understand the codebase, the pod's agentic workflow, and the permitting domain well enough to take features from spec to production without close supervision, at the pod's quality bar and without slowing the team down. Description: At Talkspace , we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission of getting therapy in the hands of everyone! We are looking for an experienced Senior Software Engineer, Tech Leadto join our Engineeringteam. The Senior Software Engineer, Tech Lead is responsible for leading software engineering teams to successfully develop and implement features, troubleshoot technical challenges, and manage product releases. This role involves planning large tasks, delegating work effectively, and ensuring high code quality through rigorous pull request reviews. The Tech Lead is accountable for delivering complex, production-ready features to QA, addressing roadblocks with persistence, and collaborating with team members to solve problems. With expertise in at least one coding area (backend, frontend, or devops), they ensure alignment with industry standards and promote a big-picture understanding of business challenges. This role also mentors junior engineers, supports hiring and training, and drives continuous improvements in code quality, system health, and QA practices. The Tech Lead fosters transparency within the team, communicates technical decisions clearly, and works closely with cross-functional teams to ensure the timely and successful completion of projects. To work at Talkspace , you need to be as passionate as we are about our work, and excited to partner with us on delivering quality mental healthcare. This is a remote position based on Eastern Time. Talkspace Headquarters is located in NYC. What You’ll Do Leadership & Project Management Leads software engineering teams by guiding feature development, troubleshooting technical issues, and managing product releases. Plans large tasks and delegates work to team members to ensure effective execution. Takes responsibility for code quality assurance, reviewing pull requests to maintain high code standards and adherence to guidelines. Ensures the delivery of complex, production-ready features to QA, minimizing bugs and improving code quality. Demonstrates persistence when facing roadblocks and collaborates with others to solve problems. Impact & Continuous Improvement Technical Expertise & Coding Skills Proficient in at least one area of coding (backend, frontend, devops) with a solid understanding of industry trends and standards. Capable of reviewing code efficiently and providing constructive feedback. Demonstrates a big-picture viewpoint with a strong understanding of business problems. Impact & Continuous Improvement Promotes transparency within the team, sharing challenges, failures, and successes. Maintains a high contribution rate to the codebase and actively addresses bugs and opens tickets for improvements. Mentors junior engineers and helps with hiring and training technical personnel. Oversees system updates, monitors system health, and ensures that all applications are up-to-date. Holds end-to-end responsibility for getting features production-ready and identifies potential risks in code. Helps ensure consistency and quality in the codebase through pull request reviews and feedback. Advocates for and enforces proper QA practices across the projects involved. Communication & Cross-Functional Leadership Collaborates with team members to identify and solve technical challenges. Creates an environment where team members feel motivated to ask questions, voice concerns, and contribute ideas. Serves as a liaison between engineering, management, and stakeholders to ensure alignment and successful project completion. Effectively communicates technical decisions through design documents, technical discussions, and comprehensive documentation. Provides mentorship to junior engineers through pairing, feedback, and regular 1:1 meetings. Communicates proactively with cross-functional teams, including product management and business teams, to address project needs and potential issues. Identifies and communicates potential project risks and requirements issues to stakeholders in a timely manner. Performs other related duties as assigned. About You Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Technology, Engineering, or Math. 6+ years of professional experience working in both react and node.js 5+ years of professional experience in software development. 3+ years of experience supporting teams or collaborating with subject matter experts, with a focus on contributing to team success and learning from leadership. Strong technical expertise and understanding of industry trends, with the ability to provide insights and assistance to the team when needed. Benefits Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision plans Pre-tax benefits: HSA/ FSA 401k Retirement Savings Program with matching up to 4% Voluntary benefits including disability, basic life or pet insurance, etc. Monthly Wellness Stipend to promote mental and physical self-care Flexible PTO and Remote First Environment Regular team events, including Wellness Workshops and Team Building Events Free access to Talkspace products for you and one household member, as well as access to a friends and family discount! Compensation At Talkspace , we believe that pay transparency during the interview process is a critical part of diversity, equity, and inclusion. Our salary bands are based on internal and external compensation benchmarks, which we regularly evaluate to ensure we pay competitively. The base salary range for this role is between $175,000 - $215,000. Within the salary bands, leveling corresponds to each candidate’s relevant experience, skills as assessed during the interview process, education, and applicable certifications. Why Talkspace ? Talkspace is the world’s leading online therapy company, serving over 2 million users looking to begin their wellness journey through tele-health. According to the World Health Organization, close to 1 billion people worldwide live with a mental disorder, and on average more than 75% with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders receive no treatment for their condition at all. Additionally, one-third of the world’s population – 2 billion people – live in countries that spend less than 1% of their health budgets on mental health. Therapy is an universal need and it's our mission here to change the world by cultivating an intentional space for people to feel supported through quality care that is simple and accessible. Combining our passion for innovation along with our desire to help others overcome the stigma behind “getting help,” we are transforming the way patients find the right care provider, making an otherwise impossible feat easily conquerable. Our network of licensed, accredited, and board-certified clinicians are increasing access to mental health for our members through a myriad of high quality therapy services: anytime and for a fraction of the price. Dedicated to our mission, we are looking for candidates that want to bring their talents into a diverse “for purpose” space. If you’re equally as passionate about making quality mental healthcare accessible to all then Talkspace is the right place for you! EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team. Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law. How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace ? Diversity Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background. Equity Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care. Inclusion Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual. Belonging Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.
