Description: Join Pigment : The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team - from Finance to HR - to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time. Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake or Siemens, use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario. With a team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software. At Pigment , we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you. We're hiring an Engineering Manager who wants to spend 80% of their time writing code, not attending management meetings. About the role Are you an experienced Software Engineer who loves writing code, solving complex technical problems and helping other engineers become better at what they do? At Pigment , our Engineering Managers are engineers first. Unlike traditional Engineering Manager positions, this role is designed for someone who wants to remain deeply involved in building software while taking on meaningful people-management responsibilities. You'll spend approximately 80% of your time designing, coding and shipping production features , with the remaining 20% dedicated to coaching engineers, running regular 1:1s, providing feedback and supporting their development. We're particularly interested in Senior Software Engineers who have naturally taken on coaching, mentoring or technical leadership responsibilities and are ready to develop further as people managers. You don't necessarily need to have held an Engineering Manager title before. What matters most is your technical ability, your experience helping others grow and your motivation to combine engineering with people leadership. You'll join Pigment 's Reporting & Collaboration community, building sophisticated frontend experiences that help customers interact with complex data, configure workflows and make better business decisions. What you'll do 🧑‍💻 Software Engineering (80%) You'll remain an active contributor to our production codebase, working alongside other engineers on challenging frontend projects. Write, review, refactor and ship production code regularly using React, TypeScript and JavaScript. Design and build sophisticated user interfaces for interacting with large datasets, including filtering, visualisation and complex configuration. Take ownership of engineering tasks and features from technical design through implementation, testing and deployment. Solve challenging problems involving frontend performance, scalability, state management and user experience. Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, debugging and architectural decisions. Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Tech Leads and Software Engineers to deliver high-quality features. Contribute to AI-powered product experiences and use modern development tools where appropriate. Maintain the same technical expectations and engineering standards as our Senior Software Engineers. You'll continue to write production code, not simply oversee the engineers who do. 📚 Coaching & People Management (20%) Alongside your engineering responsibilities, you'll help other engineers develop their skills, confidence and careers. Coach and mentor engineers, sharing technical knowledge and helping them improve their problem-solving abilities. Hold regular 1:1 meetings with your direct reports to discuss progress, challenges and career development. Provide constructive feedback, recognise achievements and support individual development plans. Help engineers establish clear goals and understand the skills required to progress. Support performance reviews and development discussions, including more challenging conversations when necessary. Work alongside Tech Leads to understand engineers' technical contributions and development needs. Help foster a collaborative engineering culture where people continuously learn from one another. At Pigment , technical leadership and people management are intentionally separated. Tech Leads own the technical direction of teams, while Engineering Managers focus on coaching and developing engineers alongside their own coding responsibilities. You'll initially focus on contributing as a Senior Engineer before gradually taking on direct reports. Who we're looking for You're an engineer first, with a genuine interest in developing people. You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and are technically operating at a strong Senior Engineer level. You're currently hands-on with production code and want coding to remain the majority of your working week. You have strong frontend development experience with React, TypeScript and JavaScript. You've built complex, scalable applications, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics or data-intensive environments. You have experience coaching, mentoring or supporting other engineers through code reviews, pairing, technical discussions or structured feedback. You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping other engineers improve. You're interested in taking ownership of 1:1s, career development and people-management responsibilities, or already have experience doing so. You're comfortable solving complex technical challenges independently while collaborating with others. You care about product quality, engineering standards and delivering meaningful value to customers. You're fluent in English. French is not required. Previous formal people-management experience is a plus, but not a requirement. We're equally interested in strong Senior Engineers who have demonstrated the ability to coach others and are ready to take the next step. Our interview process Because Engineering Managers at Pigment spend approximately 80% of their time coding, they go through the same core technical assessments as our Software Engineers. We want you to understand these expectations from the beginning. 1️⃣ Technical Screen A technical discussion including a 15-minute code refactoring exercise. AI assistance is not permitted during the refactoring exercise. 2️⃣ Live Coding A hands-on algorithmic coding interview focused on problem-solving, code quality and technical reasoning. AI assistance is not permitted. 3️⃣ System Design A discussion exploring your approach to designing software systems, evaluating technical trade-offs and solving complex engineering problems. 4️⃣ Final Interview with the EML (Engineering Manager Lead) A conversation exploring your motivation, engineering mindset, approach to coaching and alignment with Pigment 's culture and expectations. Important: Our Engineering Managers are assessed against the same senior technical engineering standards as our Software Engineers. This is a role for people who genuinely enjoy coding and want to keep doing it. Is this role right for you? You'll probably love this role if: You enjoy writing code more than spending your day in management meetings. You're a strong Senior Engineer who wants to help others grow. You want to develop people-management skills without moving away from engineering. You enjoy the challenge of balancing meaningful individual contributions with coaching responsibilities. This probably isn't the right role if: You're looking to move away from hands-on software development. You prefer managing delivery, budgets and team strategy over building software. You haven't written production code regularly for some time. You're looking for a traditional Engineering Manager position where engineering work is mainly delegated to others. At Pigment , you don't have to choose between being an excellent engineer and helping other engineers grow. Description: From Fivetran ’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven. About Us Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. ​ During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Semantic Layer team in Bengaluru. You'll own the health, delivery, and growth of the team behind MetricFlow — building and coaching a group of engineers, setting technical direction in partnership with your leads, and ensuring one of the most important projects in the modern data stack keeps shipping with quality and momentum. This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend most of your time growing people, running a healthy delivery process, and shaping strategy — but you'll stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make sound technical calls and earn the trust of a senior engineering team. You'll also be the steward of a public, community-facing open-source project, balancing the needs of internal roadmap and external contributors. About the team The Semantic Layer team owns the systems that turn dbt models into trusted, reusable business metrics. At the heart of this is MetricFlow — the open-source semantic engine that powers the dbt Semantic Layer. MetricFlow lets data teams define metrics once in code and consume them consistently across BI tools, notebooks, AI agents, and downstream applications. This team is the steward of MetricFlow as an open-source project: shipping releases, reviewing community contributions, evolving the query compiler, and ensuring it integrates cleanly with the broader dbt ecosystem. The team works at the intersection of language design, query compilation, and distributed data execution — solving problems that directly shape how thousands of organizations measure their business. What you'll do Lead, coach, and grow a team of software engineers building MetricFlow — hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, and day-to-day support. Own delivery for the Semantic Layer team: planning, prioritization, execution, and predictable shipping of high-quality software. Partner with your senior and staff engineers to set technical direction across metric definitions, query compilation, dimensional modeling, and SQL generation for multiple data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and others). Steward MetricFlow as an open-source project — set the bar for how the team triages issues, reviews external pull requests, manages releases, and engages the community on GitHub and in Slack. Collaborate with engineering leaders across the dbt platform, dbt Core, and the Semantic Layer service to ensure MetricFlow integrates seamlessly with the rest of the dbt ecosystem. Partner with product, design, and developer-relations counterparts to translate customer and community feedback into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap. Drive engineering excellence in performance, reliability, and observability of metric query execution at scale. Foster a culture of design docs, thoughtful code review, and durable engineering — shipping fast without shipping sloppy. A strong engineering foundation — you've built and shipped production software yourself and can engage credibly on architecture and technical tradeoffs with a senior team. Familiarity with the technical domain: SQL fundamentals, how analytical query engines and data warehouses execute queries, and systems that involve parsing, compilation, or transformation (query planners, DSL compilers, type systems, or rule-based engines). Solid grasp of software design principles: clean APIs, modularity, testability, and backwards compatibility — and the judgment to hold a team to them. Excellent written and verbal communication — you can explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineers, product managers, and external community members. Experience leading in a distributed, asynchronous team environment. Familiarity with dbt, MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or other semantic-layer technologies. Background in data warehousing internals, query optimization, or analytical SQL dialects. Experience with CI/CD, GitHub Actions, and release engineering for Python libraries. Exposure to building developer-facing APIs, SDKs, or CLIs. Open-source ownership: You'll lead the team behind a foundational open-source project — visible, reviewed, and used by the global data community. Description: Who we are Domino Data Lab powers model-driven businesses with its leading Enterprise AI platform trusted by over 20% of the Fortune 100. Concretely, we are building: A hardened release pipeline that produces container images meeting strict scan thresholds, with reproducible builds and minimal attack surface An automated vulnerability triage system that ingests scanner output, deduplicates findings across images and releases, routes to owners, and tracks SLA compliance—without manual triage Provenance and exploitability tooling that generates SBOMs and VEX statements on every release, so customer security questions are answered from standing artifacts rather than one-off investigations A scalable remediation practice that uses AI and automation to keep pace with the volume of findings, rather than throwing engineers at each CVE individually This is foundational work. You will replace one-off vulnerability firefighting with an automated path from scan to fix, including SBOM and exploitability statements generated on every release. You will make "we are not fixing this, and here is why" a documented engineering position backed by evidence, rather than a conversation repeated with every customer. You will set the technical direction and tooling that the next engineers on this team build on. What we look for in this role Experience shipping and maintaining software or container images into regulated, on-premises, or air-gapped environments where you cannot simply redeploy to fix a problem Deep fluency with container build systems, base image strategy, and reproducible builds, plus working knowledge of Kubernetes and Helm packaging Hands-on experience with vulnerability scanning and provenance tooling, and the judgment to distinguish a real risk from scanner noise Go and/or Python strong enough to build automation and to patch upstream open-source dependencies when no fix exists Clear technical writing. Description: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara , we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. About the role: Samsara is hiring a Senior Software Engineer II to join our Developer Experience team within the larger Developer Experience organization. We are responsible for the ‘outer-loop’ of the SDLC, with a dotted line to our sister team Dev Agents, who is responsible for the ‘inner-loop’. We are building an AI-enabled software factory that transforms how Samsara moves code from pull request to production. We use AI to eliminate repetitive steps, shorten feedback loops, and help engineers spend more time on ensuring intent. Our systems provide AI-assisted PR auto-approvals, risk-aware reviews, and automated workflows that help changes become merge-ready. We are extending that intelligence through CI and CD with AI-assisted deployment checks, production validation, and automatic rollbacks. Our goal is to enable our engineers to scale out their productivity by making the ‘outer-loop’ autonomous while keeping it safe, observable, and reliable by default. We tackle this ambitious goal from two different angles. First, we ensure our agents have the most context and their own sandbox to reduce the amount of guessing an agent needs to do in order to reach its result. Second, we ensure production is bulletproof, such that the blast radius of any issue is as minimal as possible. Our north star motto is “Merge and forget”. This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the United States. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. In this role, you will: Help scale our in-house CI/CD systems to meet the needs of a rapidly more efficient engineering organization and increasing pull-request throughput. Reduce tech debt using efficient AI workflows that would otherwise be cost prohibitive in a non-AI workflow. Design and build deployment safeguards that protect production at scale, making use of AI to monitor and fix issues. Build the observability, evaluation, and feedback systems used to improve our AI-driven automation. Serve as a thought leader for using AI to increase engineering productivity while maintaining a high bar for safety, quality, and signal over AI-generated slop. Redefine the outer loop of the SDLC by designing AI-native workflows that increase engineering throughput without compromising reliability. Push the threshold of what is possible with AI by turning emerging capabilities into safe, observable, and production-ready engineering systems. Partner with product engineering teams to reduce operational toil, and make safe, AI-enabled delivery practices easy to adopt across the company. Ensuring their specific team needs are met. Help keep Samsara at the cutting edge of AI-assisted software development by experimenting boldly, learning quickly, and converting successful experiments into platforms used across the company. Minimum requirements for the role: 8+ years of experience designing and building products in a software engineering team Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science/Engineering or equivalent practical experience 3+ years of experience working on developer experience, CICD and/or platform engineering-focused teams Experience in building AI workflows, orchestration systems or other harnesses of AI Proven track record in architecting CICD systems, build and deploy platforms, and automated response workflows, Buildkite (or equivalent BYOC software). Proven experience working on large-scale enterprise software applications Experience in building and maintaining a large organization's Software Development Life Cycle (DevEx) Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or the like) Experience in implementing AI-driven automation across the software development lifecycle (SDLC) to reduce developer friction, automate repetitive technical tasks, and accelerate time-to-delivery. Routinely applies AI tools across your workflow Experienced at writing high-quality code (Go, Python, or equivalent) focused on infrastructure, deployment, and operations challenges Experienced orchestrating multiple AI agents en-mass to tackle complex (non one-off) tasks. Strong leadership and direction setting skills. Visionary as a tech lead. Able to set a high standard for peers, and keep it. An ideal candidate also is: Forward thinking about the capabilities AI, an advocate for AI usage Experience with building in-house CICD systems Experienced with building for FedRamp, StateRamp or other compliance requirements You should apply if: You want to be on the cutting edge of AI enabled software development. You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. You want to build for scale: With over 2.3 million IoT devices deployed to our global customers, you will work on a range of new and mature technologies driving scalable innovation for customers across industries driving the world's physical operations. You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go. You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes. You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win – together. The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Description: Senior Software Engineer, Decision Science About the Company In the coming decades, our world needs far more critical minerals including copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered. KoBold is the leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects. Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations. KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery. KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi. About the Role At KoBold we believe that a modern scientific computing stack will enable systematic mineral exploration and materially improve our rate of mineral discovery. This role is a key ingredient to this strategy. As a member of our scientific computing team, you will apply decision science techniques in order to build scalable systems to help make high-speed, high-quality decisions for our mineral exploration projects. Collaborating with our exceptional team of data scientists, software engineers, and geologists, you will tackle complex scientific problems head-on and collectively pave the way for discoveries of vital energy transition metals like lithium, copper, nickel, and cobalt. Together we can shape the future of mineral exploration and contribute to building a sustainable world. Responsibilities Architect, implement, and maintain decision science libraries that will be used in KoBold’s mineral exploration analyses. Build tooling to increase the velocity of our decision making, including enabling rapid prototyping in Jupyter notebooks; build experimentation, evaluation, and simulation frameworks; turning successful R&D into robust, scalable pipelines; and organizing ML models and their outputs for repeatability and discoverability. Apply–and coach team members to use–engineering best practices such as writing robust, testable and composable code Collaborate with data scientists, geoscientists and engineers to invent the modern decision science technology for mineral exploration Occasional travel to exploration sites around the world to observe the impact of scientific computing on KoBold’s exploration products and design new technologies to further discovery. Travel is approximately twice per year depending on project needs. Qualifications Our ideal candidate will have: At least 5 years of experience in the field of decision science with a strong software engineering focus, though most great candidates will have closer to 10. Track record of building production quality data processing solutions or tooling that have delivered business value Proficiency with foundational concepts of ML, including statistical, traditional and deep-learning approaches Proficiency in Python, ideally including array-based packages such as xarray and numpy Deep experience with measured scientific data Experience in visualizing scientific data for domain experts Experience in MLops and in the making of robust ML systems Drive to increase the velocity and effectiveness of our data scientists in both experimental and production workflows Capacity to dive deep on novel challenging problems in applying decision science to mineral exploration, including understanding a complex domain of geology and mineral exploration practices as well as working with limited, disparate and noisy data sources Collaborative attitude to work with stakeholders with different backgrounds (data scientists, geoscientists, software engineers, operations) Work practices and motivation: Ability to take ownership and responsibility of large projects. Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Open to working directly with geologists in the field. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights and innovations. Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts who aren’t software developers. A strong communicator who enjoys working with colleagues across the company. Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities. Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company. Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively. What to Expect Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. Software Verification & Test Engineer Remote | East Coast Hours | Up to 10% Travel | Full Time Position Overview Crown Innovations is seeking an experienced Aviation Software Verification & Test Engineer to support the development, verification, and certification of advanced aviation navigation systems. This position will support functional, system, performance, and hardware/software integration testing for safety critical avionics applications. The selected engineer will develop and execute test cases, test scripts, procedures, and verification activities designed to evaluate system performance against defined technical and certification requirements. The role requires deep experience with DO-178C software verification and certification , avionics software and hardware testing, requirements-based verification, and safety critical aviation systems. The successful candidate must be capable of independently analyzing requirements, developing verification approaches, executing tests, evaluating results, documenting anomalies, and producing high-quality verification evidence. This position also requires hands on experience with SCADE , strong Java development experience, and familiarity with avionics certification and aircraft safety analysis. The ideal candidate is an experienced verification engineer who combines strong software development knowledge with rigorous testing discipline, exceptional attention to detail, and a thorough understanding of safety critical aviation software development and certification. Key Responsibilities Software Verification & Testing Develop, review, and execute software and system test cases, test scripts, and test procedures. Perform requirements-based verification of safety critical avionics software. Conduct functional, system, integration, and performance testing. Verify software behavior against system and software requirements. Analyze test results and identify, document, and investigate anomalies. Perform regression testing following software or requirements changes. Support software verification activities throughout the avionics development lifecycle. Ensure test artifacts are complete, traceable, repeatable, and suitable for certification evidence. Avionics Hardware & Software Integration Perform software testing on avionics hardware platforms and integrated hardware/software environments. Support hardware/software integration testing associated with navigation avionics. Evaluate system behavior under normal, abnormal, and boundary conditions. Troubleshoot software, hardware, interface, and integration issues. Support simulation, bench testing, and hardware in the loop testing environments when applicable. Collaborate with software, systems, hardware, and test engineers to isolate and resolve technical issues. DO-178C Certification & Compliance Perform verification activities in accordance with DO-178C objectives. Support preparation and maintenance of verification evidence required for avionics certification. Ensure traceability between system requirements, software requirements, test procedures, test results, and identified anomalies. Participate in requirements reviews, test reviews, peer reviews, and certification related activities. Support development and review of verification documentation and certification artifacts. Assist with identifying and resolving verification gaps or compliance issues. Requirements Analysis & Traceability Review system and software requirements for clarity, completeness, consistency, and testability. Develop test cases and procedures directly from approved requirements. Maintain bidirectional traceability between requirements and verification artifacts. Support requirements management and analysis using IBM DOORS or comparable requirements management tools. Identify ambiguous, incomplete, or conflicting requirements and coordinate resolution with engineering stakeholders. SCADE & Software Development Support Utilize SCADE within model-based software development and verification environments. Support verification of SCADE generated or model-based avionics software. Apply Java development experience to support software development, testing, automation, troubleshooting, or verification activities. Review software behavior and implementation as necessary to support test development and anomaly investigation. Collaborate with development engineers throughout verification and certification activities. Safety Critical Aviation Systems Support verification and certification activities for navigation avionics and related aircraft systems. Apply understanding of aircraft safety, system safety, and certification considerations when developing verification approaches. Support analysis of system performance and navigation related functionality. Participate in technical reviews involving software, hardware, systems engineering, and certification stakeholders. Maintain rigorous quality standards consistent with safety critical aviation development. Documentation & Technical Collaboration Develop clear and complete test procedures, test reports, verification records, and technical documentation. Document defects, anomalies, corrective actions, and test results. Communicate technical findings clearly to engineering teams and program stakeholders. Participate in peer reviews of requirements, test cases, procedures, results, and verification artifacts. Support reporting program and technical status activities as required. Minimum Required Qualifications Minimum eight years of professional software development, software verification, software testing, or related engineering experience . Minimum five years of Java development experience . Direct professional experience using SCADE . Direct experience supporting DO-178C software development, verification, testing, or certification activities . Demonstrated experience developing and executing requirements-based software test cases and procedures. Experience performing functional, system, integration, or performance testing of avionics systems. Experience testing software in conjunction with avionics hardware. Experience supporting avionics certification and testing activities. Experience with navigation avionics, aircraft navigation systems, inertial navigation systems, or closely related aviation systems. Experience with FAA certification activities, aircraft safety analysis, or other safety critical aviation development processes. Ability to analyze software and system requirements and translate requirements into executable verification activities. Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to software quality. Strong written and verbal technical communication skills. Ability to work independently within a remote engineering environment. Must be a U.S. Citizen . Preferred Qualifications Experience with IBM DOORS or comparable requirements management and traceability tools. Experience performing detailed requirements analysis. Experience with inertial navigation, GPS aided navigation, guidance, or control systems. Experience with test automation. Experience developing or maintaining automated test frameworks. Experience with hardware in the loop, simulation, or laboratory test environments. Experience with structural coverage analysis tools such as VectorCAST, LDRA, or comparable tools. Familiarity with static analysis tools. Experience with Python, C, C++, or other languages commonly used in embedded avionics verification. Familiarity with DO-254, ARP4754A, ARP4761, or related aviation development and certification standards. Experience supporting FAA or military airworthiness certification activities. Work Environment & Schedule This position is remote and requires availability during Eastern Time business hours . Travel of up to 10% may be required to support program activities, technical reviews, integration, testing, or customer needs. The position requires close collaboration with software, systems, hardware, certification, and program engineering teams. Compensation Aviation Software Verification & Test Engineer: $100,000 to $150,000 annually Compensation is determined based on experience, technical expertise, certifications, education, internal equity, and business needs. This is not about adding AI features to a traditional development process, it is a fundamental shift in how we build and ship software. Our target is Level 4 AI maturity: humans define the architecture, usage scenarios, and acceptance criteria, while AI agents autonomously write, review, and fix code. The AI Native Senior Software Engineer is a senior engineering role for builders who already work this way and can set the standard for others to follow. You will be embedded within a product stream (Rex CRM or Rex PM) as its most experienced AI-native practitioner, expected to deliver production-quality software using AI coding agents as your primary development tool, and expected to shape how the rest of the stream, and over time the wider engineering organisation, works with AI agents. You are not writing every line of code by hand, you are orchestrating AI agents to do it, auditing their output, and ensuring the result meets the architectural and quality standards of the codebase. This is explicitly not a “vibe-coding” role. At senior level, you also carry accountability for the technical decisions and AI-native practices of your stream, not just your own output. This role requires a different profile to a traditional senior software engineer. You must have the engineering maturity to recognise when AI-generated code is correct, performant, and secure, and the judgement to know when it is not, at a level that lets you set standards others follow. It is a role that requires rigor in both code and customer interactions. Our engineers are technically astute open source enthusiasts who are excited about cloud computing and are ready to join a global team charged with delivering world class services to our customers. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Employee Assistance Program Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Description: NVIDIA is redefining accelerated computing and powering the next era of artificial intelligence. Our data-center platforms bring together GPUs, CPUs, networking, systems, and software to solve some of the world’s most exciting computing problems. We are looking for a Senior System Software Engineer to join NVIDIA ’s Datacenter Performance and Power Management Software team. You will be responsible for architecting production software for datacenter power management controllers. Your work will also cover cluster- level dynamic provisioning and power-management control system technologies for next-generation data-centers. You will work at the intersection of hardware architecture, embedded firmware, device drivers, operating systems, and AI workloads. Your responsibilities will span the entire product lifecycle—from initial architectural design and pre-silicon validation through silicon bring-up, productization, and deployment in extensive data-center infrastructures. This is an outstanding chance to influence how next-generation NVIDIA GPUs provide top-tier performance, energy efficiency, and reliability. What You’ll Be Doing: Architect, build, implement, and debug data center power and performance-management software, with particular emphasis on end-to-end power management at racks and data halls. Develop real-time controllers, policies, and mechanisms that dynamically optimize performance, power, thermals, and energy efficiency under demanding data-center workloads. Drive features across the full product lifecycle: requirements, architecture, implementation, pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, productization, and production support. Collaborate with GPU architects and hardware designers to define hardware-software interfaces and influence the power-management capabilities of next-generation processors. Analyze complex interactions among workloads, clocks, voltages, power limits, thermals, telemetry, and system-level policies. Lead the investigation and resolution of complex power, performance, stability, and reliability issues spanning firmware, drivers, hardware, and platform software. Develop validation strategies and automation for functional correctness, transition latency, performance-per-watt, and robustness across operating conditions. Build clear architecture, interface, and compose specifications for new power-management features. Partner with geographically distributed architecture, ASIC, firmware, driver, validation, platform, and data-center systems teams. What We Need to See: BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent experience. At least 12+ years of extensive industry experience crafting system software, embedded firmware, device drivers, or other hardware-related production software. Strong programming skills in C, including experience developing, debugging, and maintaining complex low-level software. Deep understanding of operating-system fundamentals, device-driver architecture, embedded or real-time software, concurrency, interrupt handling, and hardware programming. Experience interpreting hardware specifications and developing software interfaces for registers, telemetry, interrupts, and control mechanisms. Strong understanding of computer architecture and hardware-software interactions. Proven ability to independently debug complex problems across multiple software and hardware layers. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of working effectively across organizational and geographic boundaries. Ways to Stand Out From the Crowd: Background with architecting, designing, or implementing datacenter provisioning, monitoring, and managing power at a CSP/NCP. Hands-on experience with GPU, CPU, accelerator, or SoC power and performance management. Background with crafting or implementing P-state selection, DVFS, clock-control, voltage-control, power-capping, thermal-management, throttling, or workload-aware control policies. Experience developing real-time feedback controllers, including reasoning about stability, responsiveness, hysteresis, latency, and noisy telemetry. Understanding of electrical and platform considerations such as voltage-frequency relationships, transient power, thermal limits, power delivery, and system-level power budgets. Description: About Forterra At Forterra , we are unleashing autonomy at scale to transform the battlefield. In an era marked by rapid technological change and evolving threats, we design for flexibility, survivability, and operational dominance. Forterra delivers weapons, sensors, and battlefield effects through integrated autonomous networks reaching operational areas faster, safer, and without placing human lives at risk. Our systems operate with distributed control, dynamic routing, and real-time responsiveness, enabling sustained advantage across complex mission environments. About the role Forterra is looking for a Lead Software Test Engineer to establish and run verification and validation for the safety critical embedded software used on our autonomous ground vehicles. This is initially an individual contributor role. You will set the software test approach, build the automation and test environments, execute the work, and maintain the evidence needed for customer and safety reviews. You will work closely with software, systems, and safety engineers to find problems early and make sure the software behaves correctly when things go wrong. As the capability grows, the role may develop into a technical lead for a small test team Someone who can build a practical software test capability from the ground up and is comfortable working directly in the code, test environments, and evidence. This person should be able to work across software, systems, and safety engineering while staying focused on finding meaningful failures and making the product more dependable What you'll do Set the verification and validation approach for safety critical embedded software from kickoff through qualification, including the test plan, test procedures, results, and reports. Turn system, software, and safety related requirements into practical tests with objective pass or fail criteria. Maintain traceability between requirements, tests, results, and anomalies. Build and maintain automated test frameworks for embedded software, including software in the loop and hardware in the loop environments. Exercise failure behavior through fault injection, timing and jitter tests, communications failures, memory faults, power and clock faults, negative tests, boundary tests, and stress tests. Use static analysis, dynamic analysis, and coverage results to find gaps and help the team close them. Prepare and maintain test evidence, including plans, procedures, results, V&V matrices, compliance matrices, anomaly records, tool qualification records, and contributions to the safety case. Work with software, systems, and safety engineers to review designs for testability, improve requirements, and support technical reviews and assessments. Provide technical guidance through test plan reviews, design reviews, pairing, and mentoring. Help establish the practices and infrastructure needed to grow a small software test capability. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered. Five or more years of experience testing embedded systems or safety critical software. Strong working knowledge of C or C++ and Python for test automation. Experience working with requirements management and requirements traceability using tools such as Jama or DOORS. Familiarity with MISRA C or MISRA C++, static analysis, and structural coverage methods such as branch coverage and MC/DC. This is one of the most senior technical roles at IREN , and it is an individual contributor role. A staff engineer is not a manager without reports. The scope is the organisation rather than a single team. The problems you take on are the ones that cross several teams, that no one team can solve alone, and that will still matter in three years. Evidence of multi-year technical judgement: a direction you set, why you set it, and how it held up afterwards. Excellent written communication. Description: About CircleCI Engineering CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them. At CircleCI , our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here. About Delivery Engineering Delivery Engineering enables CircleCI engineers to deliver quickly, confidently, and securely. We provide the tools and resources that make standard patterns and best practices simple to adopt, and we reduce toil. Our current focus is the agentic software development lifecycle: how changes are found, planned, built, reviewed, merged, and measured as AI agents take on more of the work. We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on. We're a small, very senior team, and everyone on it shapes where we go. Every improvement we make compounds across the organization. What You'll Do Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved. Shape how CircleCI builds software with agents. Help define the end-to-end agentic SDLC, from identifying a change through planning, execution, pull request, merge, and measuring impact afterward. Evaluate shared tooling and patterns, and help decide what teams standardize on. Start from how our teams actually work. Spend time with engineering teams to understand their workflows and where they get stuck. Use what you learn to drive decisions and direction that teams adopt because the work fits how they operate. Build platforms, not one-offs. Build and support shared tooling that other teams depend on, and own its adoption as much as its delivery. A tool nobody uses isn't done. Measure what matters. Instrument agent usage and outcomes so we know what improves throughput and quality and what just burns tokens. Treat cost, model choice, and reliability as design concerns. Make build-vs-buy calls. Evaluate models, vendors, and open-source tools against our needs, and choose the path that gets engineers the most leverage. Lead through influence. Write the design docs, lead technical discussions across teams, and mentor engineers across the org as they adopt agentic workflows. What You'll Bring Direct experience driving agentic developer experience efforts. You've driven an initiative that changed how an engineering organization builds software with AI agents. You can speak to what you built, how you measured its impact, how you drove adoption, and what didn't work. Hands-on depth with agentic tooling. You work daily with coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, and skills or prompt design. You know how to evaluate agent output and reason about model and token economics. A platform mindset. You've built and supported internal platforms or developer tooling that other engineers build on and rely on, and driven their adoption. Backend depth in Go. You've owned production backend services in Go, including API design, data modeling, and service integration. A track record at staff scope. 8+ years of production engineering experience, including technical decisions that spanned multiple teams and accountability for whether they landed. Decision-making grounded in your users. You build direction by listening first. You turn the needs of many teams into clear tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and bring people along. This role is open to candidates based in Europe or in the Eastern time zone. Sound like you? You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the engineers using your tools as much as the code behind them. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it with the people who'll use it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk. Responsibilities Peraton is seeking a Senior Web Developer (UI, Training Content & Adoption Tools) with instructional technology experience to support platform UI development and lead the development of web-based training content and adoption tools for a federal data integration program. You will build accessible online learning resources and the training metrics dashboard that tracks adoption across government partner offices. This is a fully remote position. The Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species . Lead the development of web-based training content and self-paced online learning modules, ensuring all materials are Section 508-compliant. Develop recorded training videos, job aids, and online help resources for government staff and general public audiences. Design and develop the Training and Adoption Metrics Dashboard, tracking usage, training completion rates, and consultation volume metrics by user group and office. Ensure all training web content meets Section 508/WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility standards Support the development of the User Testing and Training Plan, contributing web-based delivery modality specifications and content development timelines. Assist in post-deployment monitoring of the platform UI, identifying and resolving user-reported interface issues. U. S. Description: Why Thunderbird? Thunderbird is one of the world’s most trusted open-source email applications, empowering more than 20 million people globally. At Thunderbird, we build privacy-respecting communication and productivity tools that help people manage their digital lives while staying in control of their data. We are open source by design. Our products are developed transparently and in collaboration with a global community of contributors, and that same spirit shapes how we work: collaboratively, inclusively, and with a shared commitment to putting users first. Our small but growing distributed team includes more than 65 people across seven countries. As Thunderbird evolves beyond a single desktop application, we are expanding across desktop, mobile, paid services, AI offerings, and enterprise-facing work to build independent, privacy-respecting alternatives to big tech ecosystems. Our revenue model combines user donations, which help keep Thunderbird’s applications freely available, with paid services that cover the costs of hosted offerings while supporting long-term sustainability and continued innovation. A note about Thunderbird and Mozilla : Thunderbird Technologies Corporation is the nonprofit-owned company behind Thunderbird email and a growing portfolio of products. While part of the Mozilla family, Thunderbird is a separate entity from Mozilla Corporation and Mozilla Foundation with its own compensation programs, benefits, and employment policies. To learn more, visit The opportunity As a Staff Software Engineer, Services, you’ll help shape the architecture and technical direction of web-based products that extend Thunderbird beyond email. The Services team is currently focused on building offerings such as an appointment calendar and secure file storage and transfer solutions, creating valuable experiences for our users while supporting additional revenue streams for Thunderbird. This is a Staff-level individual contributor role with significant technical ownership and influence. You’ll work with designers, engineers, and community members to write code, build prototypes, solve complex problems, and make technical decisions that shape our products. You’ll take a holistic view of our code and systems, helping establish the architecture and software patterns that allow our Services products to evolve and scale. You’ll also take on broad, ambiguous problems that have a direct impact on our goals, from improving our technical architecture to helping grow Services users and subscribers. Along the way, you’ll provide technical and product direction across teams, mentor other engineers, and identify ways to make our systems and processes more sustainable, scalable, and easier to work with. What you’ll do Lead the technical architecture of new Services products, taking ownership of complex projects and identifying improvements that strengthen our systems as they evolve. Write code, build prototypes and experiments, and contribute throughout the development lifecycle, from planning and testing through implementation, monitoring, and maintenance. Help establish software patterns and make technical decisions across our Services products, including investigating and proposing technology choices. Build and evolve analytics and infrastructure that help the team use user-generated data to inform decisions. Architectural direction sits with the Staff Architect, and the AI Engineers own the agents. You are the builder: you take features from the design doc to production, end to end, and you make them fast, observable, and reliable. Implement typed, versioned API contracts and evolve them without breaking clients. Own authentication, authorization, and multi-tenant access control across the portal. Own the read path and performance Own the read path over analytical data: data modeling, query plans, pagination, batching, caching, and consistency trade-offs. Set and defend performance budgets. Profile services, reduce tail latency (p95, p99), and optimize cost per request. Run load and capacity tests before launches, and use the results to make design decisions. Define SLIs and SLOs, alerts, and dashboards for the components you own, and take part in on-call. Diagnose and fix reliability issues, and lead incident response and blameless postmortems. Establish safe rollout practices: feature flags, canary releases, and fast rollback. Raise the team's technical bar through code review, pairing, and standards for testing, observability, and safe rollout. Use coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex as part of your workflow, and review generated code against tests, types, and contracts. What you'll need: Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field. A master's degree or PhD is a plus. Relevant experience designing, building, and operating distributed backend services in production, across coding standards, code review, build, automated testing, deployment, and operations. A track record of building features end-to-end and owning them in production. Relevant experience in software design for reliability and scale, on both new and existing systems. Deep command of at least one high-performance language, such as Java/Kotlin, Go, Rust, C++, or C#, including its memory model, concurrency model, and runtime. Ability to work productively in Python, the language of the current services. Hands-on experience with observability in production: metrics, tracing, logging, SLOs, and tools such as OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Grafana, or Prometheus. Proven experience with performance work: profiling, query optimization, caching strategies, and load testing. Production depth in distributed systems: timeouts, retries, idempotency, partial failure, streaming (SSE, WebSockets), and decisions based on tail latency (p95, p99). Relevant experience delivering full stack to production with TypeScript and a modern web framework. Day-to-day fluency with coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex, including critical review of generated code. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to discuss architecture and trade-offs in depth. Advanced communication in English; Spanish is a plus. Nice to have: Experience with serving layers for analytical data (OLAP, columnar stores, semantic layers) or with data platform integration. Experience integrating applications with LLM or agent services as a consumer. Experience with B2B, multi-country, or multi-tenant products. Experience with cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP), containers, and Kubernetes. More about you: You are a builder: you like taking a feature from a blank page to production and owning it from then on. You spend most of your time writing, reviewing, and operating code. You treat observability and performance as part of the feature, not something added afterward. You influence architecture with evidence: measurements, prototypes, and explicit trade-offs. You go from the API to the interface when the feature needs it. You use tests, types, and contracts as the guardrails for your code and for generated code. You work well on a staff-level team where everyone operates what they ship. Experience with automation and systems integration tools such as Zapier, Make, or n8n, and email marketing or landing page platforms such as ConvertKit or Klaviyo. Experience implementing website security best practices to protect client sites from vulnerabilities and downtime. AI literacy, including experience using tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to support development work and improve workflow efficiency. Description: About Kadince Kadince (pronounced cadence) is a fully remote (must live in the USA) software company founded in 2013. In a nutshell, we build tools to help compliance and marketing professionals at financial institutions do their jobs more efficiently. Kadince has been profitable for several years (we’re fans of making more than we spend). We’re bootstrapped, which means we don’t have investors. So our owners answer to no one. And they aren’t just giving us commands from their vacation homes waiting to cash their next check. They’re fellow team members and in the trenches with us. Why We’re Hiring After our team members, our customers are our most important focus. As our customer base grows, so does our team. We’re dedicated to giving each customer the best experience possible, which means having enough people to take care of all their needs. We’re growing quickly and so are the needs of our customers. That’s why we’re increasing the size of our development team. Who We Want to Hire To be a web developer at Kadince we prefer you have 5+ years of experience. This experience has given you an understanding of basic database driven web applications and a proficient knowledge of the MVC pattern. You understand that software development is all about the end-user (again, we really care about our customers). You have a desire to continually learn and improve your development skills. We love giving team members opportunities to improve their skills, whether through online courses, workshops, or learning from others. You’re able to adapt quickly to new environments, are organized and focused, can look beyond current constraints (you know, forest through the trees), and can provide solutions to complex problems. Simply put, we need a problem solver, not a taskmaster. Our vision, mission, and core values should resonate with you. That’ll be crucial to your success and happiness if you join the Kadince team. Let’s Geek Out If you’re geeky like our dev team (hopefully you are), you probably want to know more about our tech-stack. Outside of our dev team, we’re not really sure what most of this means, but we sure hope you do. Technologies/Frameworks Ruby on Rails GraphQL Postgres Redis ReactJS Minitest Cypress DevOps Kubernetes Helm Docker CircleCI Other Tools Jira Rubymine Sentry Logrocket Wooly Bugger Our Vision and Mission Our vision and mission aren’t something we hung on the office wall and forgot about. Seriously, we don’t have an office, let alone a wall to hang them on. But our vision, mission, and core values sit on the desks of each of our team members. And we discuss them regularly in our meetings. Your goals and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) will be developed to ensure you’re working to help us achieve our vision and mission. Our vision and mission are what get us up each morning. They, in addition to our core values, help us make decisions. Vision - Setting the standard for operating a great software company. We’re big fans of author Jim Collins and his best-selling book, Good to Great (bonus points if you’ve read it). While there are lots of good software companies out there, we want to be one of the great ones. The first word of our vision is also significant. To go “high school English class” on you, the present participle “setting” illustrates that we’re not looking to set the standard and then be done, but that the standard is always moving and we’re always chasing it. We continually stop to recognize the awesome things we’ve done and then look for ways to do them even better. Mission - Building the best software for compliance and marketing professionals at financial institutions. As Jim Collins taught in his Hedgehog Concept (told you we think he’s great—pun intended), great companies need to determine what they can be the best at in the world and focus on that. There are so many things we could solve as a software company, but we’ve found what we think we can be the best in the world at and we stick to it every day. Our Core Values Our core values remind us who we are. They also guide us in the decisions we make. They’re listed in order of importance. If we have a question when making a decision about people, for example, we look to the core value above it to make our decision. Integrity - We’re honest with ourselves and others. People - We understand that people are the foundation of Kadince and we act accordingly. Care - We love what we do and do it consistently and intentionally to the best of our abilities. Remarkability - We provide remarkable experiences to all who come into contact with Kadince . Growth - We accept yesterday and improve today. What a Day in the Life of a Web Developer Looks Like Your day starts with a development team meeting where you go through announcements, sync up projects, and discuss any potential issues. After the meeting, you put your head down and work on your assigned tickets in Jira. You spend the first part of the day reviewing your notes and prioritizing tasks for the junior developers. You make sure that you and the other developers are working on the most important tasks first, but you’re free to choose which ones you work on. For lunch, you meet a friend at the cafe near his work. You haven’t seen your friend for a few months, so you talk about life and your careers. You can’t help but feel very lucky for the freedom you have to take a long lunch break and meet your friend, as he has to hurry back to the office and get working right at the hour. Back at home, you continue working on tickets in Jira. At one point a junior web developer calls you on Slack and asks how to fix an issue. You expertly show him the process and he thanks you for being so helpful. You notice that another developer has been really on top of it today, so you mention them in the company Slack channel and thank them for being so awesome. Many of your team members respond to your shoutout with party emojis and hearts. In the afternoon your team has a standup meeting where you discuss what projects you’re all working on and whether there’s anything anyone can do to help. Your leader points out one of the awesome projects you’re working on and thanks you for being so attentive to the users’ needs. After the standup you do some QA and manually test a couple of the changes your team made today. You write automated tests to ensure the functionality that was just worked on. You find one little bug, which you log and then fix easily. You finish up your day by taking a look at tomorrow’s schedule and planning accordingly. When and Where You’d Work and What You’d Work On Kadince is a principle-based company, which means we focus on principles, not policies. You’ll work with your leader, Aaron Venezia, each week to review your goals/KPI and what you’ve been working on. You’ll meet regularly with the Development team to learn, keep projects on track, and ensure that goals/KPIs are being reached. While we aren’t super particular about when and where you work, you’ll need to work around the schedules of other team members to ensure that goals stay on track and nothing falls through the cracks. Overall, your schedule needs to help you achieve our vision and mission and demonstrate our core values. After all, this is a full-time job, and we treat it that way! At Kadince , work won’t tie you down to one location. You’ll be free to travel or relocate as you get the itch to try somewhere new. Want to spend a month abroad, working from a hotel and exploring the rest of the time? Go ahead. Just make sure you have a reliable high-speed internet connection (as if you would go anywhere without it anyway) and turn on the blurry filter during video calls so we don’t get jealous. We seriously get jealous. One of our teammates recently had zebras running around in the background of a video call during a team meeting. Come to find out he was working from the deck of his hotel at the Animal Kingdom in Disney World. Even though we were jealous, we thought it was pretty cool. Who You’d Be Working With We have over 50 team members (which makes us really happy since Kadince was started by two people in their basements). If hired, you’ll probably work with each team member in one way or another. Some of the people you’ll work with most frequently are: Aaron makes sure that Kadince software runs smoothly and that any problems are addressed quickly and efficiently. When it comes to software wizards, he’s the Dumbledore of web developers (but really, he wishes he was Voldemort). He’s been here since nearly the beginning of Kadince , so he’s seen it all. Aaron loves to go skiing and mountain biking, as well as play video games and pinball (can you beat him?). He’s very proud of the fact that he’s his tiny dog’s favorite person, and he has a strange passion for curly fries. Bernardo (better known around here as Beans) has been a web developer at Kadince since 2014. He’s originally from Chile, but has lived in Utah since he was 12. He loves to code, play video games, spend time with his wife, kids, and dogs. He also loves to learn new things. If he could do anything in the world he would go to space (although technically that’s not in this world, now is it?). Luis is a senior web developer and has worked for Kadince since 2019. He likes to hike, run, and be outdoors. Luis is fun and gets along with everyone, so feel free to joke around and have a good time. Just don’t play Rocket League with him. He WILL beat you. Actually, do play, lots of the other developers do. And if you’re lucky, he might share his grandma’s tamales with you. Benefits Since we’re a remote company, we don’t offer office snacks and ping pong tables. But if you’re a fan of “core benefits” that bring great rewards and peace of mind, you’ll like what we have to offer. Competitive pay, 401(k) matching, generous paid leave, insurance (medical, dental, vision, life, short-term disability), and a flex spending account. Yeah, it’s pretty great... And we love to spoil our team. We celebrate big events with you, like birthdays and work anniversaries, so you can expect some pretty fun gifts. We once sent some high-quality lip balm to each team member so we could all play a prank on Scott, our Director of Product. We’re fun like that. And this year we’re giving every team member the last week of the year off (we like to spread holiday cheer). How to Apply Applicants who stand out are those who are interested in working for Kadince , not just applying for as many positions as possible or trying to keep unemployment benefits. We’ve seen it all. No kidding, we once had someone ask us in an interview what the name of our company is. Needless to say, we could tell that person wasn’t really passionate about joining our team. When applying to Kadince , please send us a PDF of your resume. The questions below are your opportunity to tell us why you would be a great fit for the position. Take advantage of this time. Seriously, sell yourself! Thank you for your interest in Kadince . We look forward to reviewing your application. This position is open to candidates living in AL, AK, AZ, AR, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, IA, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, MS, MO, NE, NV, NH, NM, NC, ND, OH, OK, PA, RI, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WV, WI, and WY. Kadince , Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Salary: $70,000-$120,000 Originally posted on Himalayas

A good eye for design and attention to detail. The ability to work independently, manage priorities, and communicate clearly in English. Nice to have: experience with WordPress, Ruby on Rails, or a modern frontend framework. Role mission Build, optimize, and scale the digital experiences that help customers discover, evaluate, and engage with Ivanti . As a Full Stack Web Developer, you’ll turn marketing strategy and creative ideas into fast, secure, accessible, and high-performing web experiences used across Ivanti ’s global digital presence. What to expect We’re looking for a hands-on Full Stack Web Developer with strong front-end expertise to help evolve ivanti.com and the digital experiences that support our customers throughout their journey. You’ll work across the full web stack, from polished front-end experiences and interactive content to C#/.NET applications, CMS functionality, APIs, SQL Server, integrations, and deployment pipelines. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys building things that people actually see and use, while also being comfortable getting under the hood to solve complex technical problems. You’ll partner closely with Creative and Marketing teams and have the autonomy to take work from concept and implementation through launch and production support. You don’t need to come from a perfectly modern tech stack. We’re looking for someone who can work pragmatically across established, legacy, and modern technologies while helping us continuously improve how we build for the web. What you’ll do Build experiences: Develop responsive, accessible, high-quality website experiences using C#, ASP.NET, MVC, Razor, JavaScript, HTML, CSS/SCSS, APIs, and SQL Server. Bring creative ideas to life: Partner closely with Creative to turn approved designs into polished, responsive, cross-browser experiences. Create reusable solutions: Build components, templates, campaign pages, interactive tools, and major website experiences that scale beyond one-off projects. Develop rich interactions: Create engaging web experiences using JavaScript and GSAP, including responsive animations and scroll-based interactions. Own the full web stack: Work across CMS configuration, application code, APIs, databases, forms, integrations, routing, caching, redirects, and third-party services. Support our digital ecosystem: Help integrate analytics, Google Tag Manager, browser data layers, consent and privacy tooling, and other marketing technologies. Ship confidently: Contribute to Git-based development, code reviews, Azure DevOps pipelines, testing, releases, launches, and production support. Solve complex problems: Diagnose issues across front-end code, .NET applications, databases, APIs, IIS, Azure services, Cloudflare, caching, integrations, and traffic routing. Own your work: Take projects from investigation and estimation through implementation, testing, deployment, and production support, communicating risks and dependencies along the way. Build smarter with AI: Use tools such as GitHub Copilot to accelerate development, debugging, documentation, refactoring, and code review while ensuring quality, security, performance, and maintainability. What you’ll bring We’re looking for someone who combines strong web development fundamentals with curiosity, ownership, and a practical approach to solving problems. Professional experience building and supporting production websites or web applications in a full-stack development role. Strong experience with C#, ASP.NET, ASP.NET MVC, Razor, JavaScript, HTML, CSS/SCSS, and SQL Server. Strong front-end skills, particularly responsive development, accessibility, cross-browser compatibility, and translating designs accurately into code. Experience working with a CMS or content-managed website environment. Experience with Kentico Xperience is a plus. Confidence working across multiple layers of a web application, from CMS configuration and browser code through APIs, application logic, and databases. Experience with APIs, integrations, forms, HTTP behavior, caching, Git, deployment pipelines, and production releases. Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to get up to speed quickly with unfamiliar systems. Clear communication skills and the ability to explain technical considerations and trade-offs to non-technical partners. Experience using GitHub Copilot or another AI coding assistant as part of a professional development workflow. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Nice to have You don’t need to check every box, but experience in any of the following would be valuable: ASP.NET Web Forms Kentico Xperience 13 or Xperience by Kentico Vue, Nuxt or TypeScript Tailwind CSS, jQuery, vanilla JavaScript or GSAP Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code and GitHub Azure DevOps, IIS, Azure Functions or Azure Storage Cloudflare, CDN configuration, caching or traffic routing Technical SEO, website performance and accessibility Consent management, analytics or tag management B2B, enterprise technology or marketing-focused websites Why this role matters The corporate website sits at the center of Ivanti ’s digital presence, connecting customers with our products, content, campaigns, and brand. In this role, you’ll help us move faster, build better experiences, and strengthen the technical foundation behind our digital marketing ecosystem. Your work will improve website performance and reliability, expand reusable capabilities for Marketing, and help us deliver secure, accessible, engaging experiences at scale. Why Ivanti ? Friendly flexible working model: Empower excellence whether you’re at home or in the office and support work-life balance . Competitive compensation & total rewards : Including health, wellness, and financial plans tailored for you and your family. Global, diverse teams: Collaborate with talented people from 23+ countries. Learning & development: Grow your skills with access to best-in-class learning tools and programs. Equity & belonging: We value every voice. Your story helps inform our solutions for a changing world.
