We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home. Our Impact Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts. About the Role: You are the technical owner of every pixel a Commerce merchant or shopper sees. You also raise the frontend bar for all of HighLevel . The role has two horizons. Commerce first. You set the architecture. You write the standards. You review the code. You hire the team. You hold the line on performance, accessibility, and quality while engineers and their coding agents ship into Commerce every day. Then HighLevel . Commerce is greenfield. That makes it the place to prove what excellent frontend engineering looks like at HighLevel . What works in Commerce becomes a shared capability, so every organization benefits. The central frontend platform team is your closest partner on both horizons. They own the shared foundation. You are their most demanding customer and one of their strongest contributors. You bring Commerce requirements early. You co-design solutions with them. You upstream what Commerce builds, so HighLevel keeps one foundation. This is an individual contributor role at staff level. You lead through design documents, code, reviews, and the people you grow. You will write production code every week. The bar is high. A storefront that loads in six seconds loses the sale. A checkout a screen reader cannot use excludes a customer and breaks the law in some markets. An architecture that couples every team slows every one of them. A pattern that stays inside one organization helps only that organization. You own all four problems. Responsibilities: First 90 days Publish the Commerce frontend standard: architecture, state, data fetching, testing, accessibility, and performance. Every Commerce team adopts it. Instrument real-user monitoring on every Commerce surface. Publish field metrics for LCP, INP, and CLS per surface, with an owning team for each. Review frontend pull requests across Commerce. Raise the quality of every one you touch, and write down the patterns so reviews scale beyond you. Map the central frontend platform roadmap against Commerce needs. Agree a working contract with that team: what the platform provides, what Commerce builds, and how requests and contributions flow both ways. Set up a standing design review with the central platform team, so Commerce decisions and platform decisions stay aligned. Produce a frontend hiring plan: how many engineers, at what levels, and in what order. First 6 months Ship the architecture that lets every Commerce team build and deploy its surfaces independently, with enforced module boundaries. Build it on the central platform's foundation wherever one exists, and close gaps jointly with that team. Put performance and bundle budgets in CI for every Commerce route. A regression fails the build. Make accessibility a gate: automated checks in CI and manual audits on checkout and storefront flows against WCAG 2.2 AA. Land typed, generated API clients end to end, so a backend contract change breaks at compile time. Contribute at least one Commerce-built capability to the central platform, adopted by another organization. Hire and onboard the first Commerce frontend engineers. First 12 months Commerce storefronts meet "good" Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile in field data, on mid-range mobile devices. Checkout and storefront pass a WCAG 2.2 AA audit. Backend engineers ship frontend features that meet the standard without your direct involvement. Coding agents across Commerce follow the frontend standard by default, through shared instructions, skills, and review gates you designed. Commerce is HighLevel 's reference implementation for frontend excellence. Its standards, performance budgets, and agent guidance reach other organizations through the central platform. You lead or co-lead HighLevel -wide frontend decisions with the central platform team, written as RFCs other organizations build on. The Commerce frontend team runs on its own. You spend your time on the next hardest problem at HighLevel . Requirements: You have 9+ years of experience in building frontend systems You have built commerce surfaces at scale: storefronts, checkout, or point of sale. You have built or led a design system consumed by many teams, and shipped breaking changes through it safely. You have used ConnectRPC, gRPC-Web, or protocol buffers from the browser. You can read and write Go well enough to build or review a backend-for-frontend. You contribute to open source, web standards discussions, or the frontend community. You have taught backend engineers to ship good frontend code. You have contributed to a shared frontend platform or design system used by several product organizations. Our Stack & Direction Frontend. Vue.js across HighLevel . TanStack Query for server state. Webpack and Rspack for builds, with micro-frontends where teams need independent deploys. Contracts. ConnectRPC with protocol buffers from the browser to the backend. The client calls typed functions and receives typed responses. No hand-written REST clients. Backend. Go services on Kubernetes, with Postgres as the primary store. Backend-for-frontend layers run inside the cluster, close to the services they call. Rendering. Static generation where content allows it, client-side rendering for interactive surfaces, and a backend-for-frontend to aggregate data. You will challenge and refine this direction with evidence. Engineering practice. Every engineer works with coding agents. Standards live as written documents, shared agent instructions, and review gates. What you bring on day one: Scope. You have owned frontend architecture across several teams for a multi-quarter effort. Other teams still build on decisions you made. You can show us the before and after. Platform partnership. You have worked with a central platform team as both a consumer and a contributor. You influence roadmaps you do not own. You negotiate scope with evidence. You land changes in shared code that many organizations depend on, without breaking them. You have taken a standard from one team and made it company-wide. The browser platform. You know the rendering pipeline, the event loop, and what makes a long task. You follow new platform features through Baseline and MDN, and you have shipped some of them. You reach for the platform before a library, and you have deleted dependencies because the browser made them unnecessary. Performance. You diagnose with field data, performance traces, and network waterfalls. You have moved Core Web Vitals in production and kept them there with budgets and ownership. You can explain where every millisecond of a page load goes, from DNS to interaction. Architecture for many teams. You have designed systems where many teams deploy independently into one product. You know module federation, native ES modules, import maps, monorepos, and when each one fits. You know what each costs: duplicate dependencies, runtime integration bugs, build infrastructure. You pick deliberately. Data and contracts. You design how the client talks to the server: backend-for-frontend layers, typed RPC contracts, caching, and invalidation. You understand why twenty sequential calls over the public internet cost seconds, and how to collapse them. Accessibility. You build with semantic HTML first and add ARIA only where semantics fall short. You know WCAG 2.2, colour contrast requirements, and keyboard and screen reader behaviour. You have led an accessibility audit and fixed what it found. Security. You treat user-generated content as hostile. You know XSS, content security policy, sandboxed rendering, and supply chain risk in the npm ecosystem. Code review. Your reviews make engineers better. You find the race condition before the naming nit. You turn repeated feedback into lint rules, patterns, and documentation. AI-assisted engineering. You use coding agents every day with discipline. You write the context, specs, and skills that make agent output match the standard. You verify generated code with tests and review. You have a view on how teams keep a codebase understandable when everyone generates three times more code. Writing. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts. About the Role: We're looking for a Staff Front-End Engineer to own the architecture of our platform UI. This is a core platform role, not a feature role — you'll own the layer every other team builds on: the application shell, our module federation topology, the shared component library, build tooling, and the performance bar that applies across every surface of the product. You'll stay hands-on with code and architecture while setting technical direction across multiple teams and leading multi-quarter migrations without stalling feature delivery. Our stack is primarily Vue 3; strong engineers from React, Angular, or Svelte backgrounds are welcome, and existing Vue experience is a plus. Responsibilities: Failure Isolation: Design so a broken or slow remote degrades one surface, not the whole application — with fallbacks, timeouts, and the observability to identify which remote caused an incident. Release Strategy: Own the deployment and versioning story for independent releases, including contract testing across host/remote boundaries, staged rollout, and fast rollback of a single remote. Load Performance: Attack bundle size and dependency-graph bloat through code splitting, shared-chunk strategy across federated remotes, preloading/prefetching, and caching/CDN strategy. Runtime Performance: Attack main-thread cost through long-task analysis, reactivity and re-render cost, list virtualization, and memory leak diagnosis in long-lived sessions. You're the person engineers escalate production-only regressions and render thrash to. Performance Measurement: Define the metrics that matter (Core Web Vitals, INP, route transition time), instrument them in real-user monitoring, and enforce budgets in CI so regressions are caught before they ship. Quality Bar: Set and enforce accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), internationalization, and cross-browser support through automated checks, not documentation alone. Technical Leadership: Write proposals that build genuine consensus, review designs and code where decisions are expensive to reverse, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers across the org. Requirements: 9+ years of front-end development experience. Expert-level JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with a first-principles understanding of the browser — rendering/layout, the event loop, network/caching, and memory. Deep production experience with a modern component framework. Primarily Vue 3 (Composition API); strong React, Angular, or Svelte experience is welcome if you're willing to go deep on Vue. Demonstrated architectural ownership — you've defined a front-end architecture and moved a real codebase from one state to another without freezing feature work. Hands-on production experience with micro-frontends or module federation, including the failure modes. Equivalent experience decomposing a large monolith by other means also considered. Proven track record optimizing large-scale, complex web applications. Be ready to walk through a specific example with numbers. Experience with modern build tooling at scale (Vite, Webpack, Rspack, Turborepo, or Nx), with enough depth to debug the build when it breaks. Working knowledge of accessibility as an engineering discipline — semantics, focus/keyboard behavior, ARIA where genuinely needed, screen reader testing. Strong written communication. On a remote-first, async team, most of your influence travels as design docs, RFCs, and PR descriptions. A track record of mentoring engineers and driving change across teams you don't manage. Nice to have: familiarity with Node.js, server-side rendering, and open-source contributions. What You'll Lead: The target architecture for our front-end, and the migrations that get us there — sequenced into reversible steps, driven with codemods and adoption metrics, agreed across teams rather than imposed on them. The application shell and its contracts: bootstrapping, routing, auth-aware navigation, error and loading boundaries, and cross-application state. Our module federation topology: host and remote boundaries, shared dependency and singleton management, and version skew between independently deployed remotes. The shared component library and design system implementation, with APIs that are hard to misuse and safe to version. EEO Statement: The company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About the Project Purpose The Australian National Species List Website project will deliver high-quality online user interfaces to taxonomic and descriptive information about Australias unique plants, animals, fungi and other living things. Context Background: The Australian National Species List (auNSL) provides an authoritative source of information about the naming and classification of Australias unique plants, animals, fungi and other living things. The auNSL is a key resource supporting the management and conservation of, and research on, Australias biodiversity. Data from the auNSL supports a range of national biodiversity data infrastructures including the Atlas of Living Australia, the Terrestrial Ecosystem Research Network, and the Biodiversity Data Repository. The auNSL runs on dedicated software infrastructure built and maintained by the Biodiversity Informatics team within the Biodiversity Conservation & Knowledge section of Parks Australia as part of the Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research (CANBR) a joint agreement with CSIRO. Environment: The Australian National Species List infrastructure (NSLi) is delivered via an AWS cloud environment. The NSLi is built on a PostgreSQL database, has a data entry interface (Rails), and provides machine access through GraphQL and REST APIs delivered via Hasura as JSON. Assumptions: The software developer will work with the Biodiversity Informatics team under the direction of the team manager. The user-interface will be built using a suitable frontend framework (e.g. React, Next.js, Vue.js, Rails etc) and containerised for deployment (ECS, Fargate). auNSL data will be integrated into the frontend via the GraphQL and REST APIs. An open-source headless CMS (e.g. strapi) will be implemented for descriptive information and other display assets to be used on the webpages. At the end of the engagement the Biodiversity Informatics team will be able to take on the further development and maintenance of the delivered infrastructure. Description: About HighLevel : HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes. To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently. Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability. Our People With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home. Our Impact Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts. About Commerce & Payments Team: The Commerce & Payments team is a newly formed organization to add HighLevel ’s evolving capabilities and make it both a Commerce Platform and a surface where our customers can perform their sales motions for their products. Building Catalogs, subscriptions, fulfillment , payment processing engines, inventory mgmt, pricing, documents/contracts and more to enable our SMBs to increase their revenue will be the core focus of the org. Hardly any tech debt, mostly green field work working closely with product folks to build, ship and refine our Commerce offerings makes this an exciting place to learn, engage and thrive. About the Role: We're building a global commerce platform to power $1T+ in annual transactions for millions of SMEs. As an SDE II on the frontend, you'll build the surfaces that customers and their buyers touch: storefronts, checkout, catalog, subscription management, invoices and contracts. These surfaces carry money. They get embedded inside other people's experiences. They run on slow phones and flaky networks in 150+ countries. A layout shift shows up in someone's conversion rate, and a 300ms regression shows up in someone's revenue. This role is for engineers who obsess over frontend craft and have the depth to back it up. If you already know why your bundle is that size, where your hydration cost goes, and what your service worker does on a cache miss, we want to talk to you. Responsibilities: Build and ship the commerce surfaces: storefronts, checkout, catalog, subscription management, invoices and documents Embed our experiences inside other experiences — module federation, iframes and white-label hosts that stay isolated, load fast and degrade gracefully Own performance budgets end to end: Core Web Vitals, bundle size, render cost, hydration, main-thread work. Measure them in CI and defend them Build installable, offline-tolerant PWAs with service workers, considered caching strategies and background sync Deliver WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility and full localisation across languages, currencies, tax and address formats, and RTL layouts Instrument the client with real-user monitoring and OpenTelemetry so regressions surface before customers report them Collaborate with PM/Design and mentor junior engineers Requirements: 2+ years building and operating production frontend applications Deep Vue.js knowledge: the reactivity model, component composition, rendering behaviour, and the runtime cost of each choice A visible performance habit. You live in Lighthouse, Chrome DevTools and the performance profiler, and you can walk us through a regression you found, measured and fixed Service workers and caching strategy: precaching, runtime caching, versioning, invalidation, and offline behaviour that stays correct Client state management and local caching at scale (TanStack Query or equivalent): cache keys, staleness, invalidation, optimistic updates Accessibility as a build-time discipline: semantics, focus management, keyboard paths, screen reader behaviour, WCAG 2.2 AA Internationalisation and localisation: message extraction, plurals, locale-aware currency and date formatting, RTL Modern frontend tooling and module federation (Rspack, Vite), plus bundle analysis and code splitting An eye for craft. You notice the four-pixel misalignment, the janky scroll, and the layout shift that only appears on a throttled connection, and you fix all three Comfortable consuming typed backend contracts (ConnectRPC/protobuf) and reasoning about API contracts and error states Excellent debugging and problem-solving skills Tech Stack: Frontend: Vue.js, Rspack, Module Federation, TanStack Query Client platform: Service workers/PWA, OpenTelemetry, Vite, ESLint Backend contracts: Go, ConnectRPC, Buf Cloud: GCP (GKE), Pub/Sub EEO Statement: The company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Description: Atmosera empowers businesses to redefine what's possible with modern technology and human expertise. Our exceptional experience across Applications, Data & AI, DevOps, Security, and the Microsoft Azure platform enables organizations to accelerate innovation, enhance security, and optimize operational agility. As a Microsoft Partner with nine specializations, GitHub AI Partner of the Year, a member of the GitHub Advisory Board, and a member of the prestigious Microsoft Intelligent Security Association (MISA), Atmosera expertly delivers cutting-edge, integrated solutions that deliver business value. You are joining us as a front-end web developer who will own and evolve the user interfaces for our internal tools. Alongside that primary focus, you will grow into full ownership of our Power BI reporting, building on solid, hands-on Power BI experience to take on report and dashboard delivery. Your day-to-day will involve building and improving user interfaces first and foremost, while growing into ownership of our Power BI reports, dashboards, and report-deployment process — all aimed at making our internal tools more usable and our reporting reliable, consistent, and easy to maintain. Required Skills • Years of Experience — 5+ years of experience • Role-Specific Mastery — Strong, hands-on front-end web development skills (React or similar) as your primary craft, complemented by solid, hands-on Power BI experience — enough to take on full ownership of report and dashboard delivery. • Operational Excellence — Working knowledge of the Power BI data layer (semantic models, DAX, Power Query/M) and SQL, with comfort learning and eventually owning an existing Python-based deployment/automation codebase. • Communication — Strong written and spoken English, with the fluency to collaborate clearly with technical, non-technical, and client-facing colleagues. • Collaboration — Experience partnering with engineers and cross-functional or client-facing teams to make sure the right data is surfaced in the right way, and comfort taking over and improving an inherited platform rather than only building from scratch. • Problem Solving — A strong eye for design and usability, and the judgment to improve the robustness of an existing deployment process by reducing brittle, manual steps. Preferred Qualifications • Power BI Projects (PBIP) — Experience with Power BI Projects and TMDL semantic-model definitions. • Power Platform — Experience with the Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate). • Design Tooling — Experience with design systems, component libraries, or UX tooling (e.g., Figma) to keep interfaces consistent and polished. • Azure Ecosystem — Familiarity with Azure Resource Graph, Log Analytics/KQL, and Microsoft Sentinel. What Success Looks Like We measure success by results and alignment. Here is how we define a "win" for this role over your first year: After 90 Days • The Foundation — You have developed a strong understanding of the existing front-end codebase, and are already building and updating individual Power BI reports yourself as part of your onboarding. • The Integration — You have built working relationships with Engineering and with the client-facing teams who rely on your reporting output, and are fielding Power BI requests directly. • The Contribution — You have independently delivered several Power BI report or dashboard updates, and shipped your first UI improvement. After 1 Year • Your Impact — You have taken full ownership of Power BI reporting — including report delivery and the report-deployment process — while also shipping measurable improvements to our internal tools' UI. • Your Growth — You have become the team's go-to owner for Power BI reporting and a strong, independent contributor on the front-end codebase. • Your Influence — You have defined and documented standard measures, naming conventions, and templates that made reporting consistent across programs and clients, and helped shape a new internal configuration-management interface from the ground up. How We Show Up These 'Core Three' represent the heartbeat of Atmosera . They are the behaviors and attributes we align to every day, defining how we interact, solve problems, and celebrate our wins together. This is simply who we are at our best. • Humble (Low Ego, High Impact) — We share credit easily, admit when we're wrong, and view every mistake as a data point for growth. • Hungry (Internal Drive) — We have a natural bias for action. We don't wait for permission to solve a problem or find a better way to do things. • Mindful (Intentional Awareness) — We are conscious of our impact on the team. We listen more than we speak and respond to challenges with empathy and situational awareness. Our Interview Process We value your time and aim for transparency. Our typical interview process looks like this: 1. Talent Screen: (30 mins) A conversation about your background and the role mission. 2. The Impact & Attributes Assessment: (60 mins) The "What" (Required Skills and Core Capabilities). This stage will require a Live coding challenge. 3. Collaborator Loop: (45 mins) The "How" (Cultural DNA and The Core Three). Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: About Virtualitics Virtualitics is the category leader in AI-native readiness applications for defense, government, and critical infrastructure. Our team is excited to find our next Senior Frontend Engineer to join the company. As a Senior Frontend Engineer at Virtualitics , you will own the frontend of our next-generation application platform: the shared app shell, component library, hooks, and typed API client that every customer project team builds their product on. You will design the component APIs other engineers reach for first, decide how the platform handles auth, layout, theming, data fetching, and real-time updates, and keep all of it fast, accessible, and secure enough for defense networks. You will work alongside backend, AI, and DevSecOps engineers, and with the project teams shipping to defense and government customers. This is a chance to shape how a platform looks and behaves before it hardens, and to see your work in front of analysts and decision-makers within weeks. Our frontend is React and TypeScript, built with modern tooling and shipped as versioned packages that project teams build on. We use Material UI alongside an in-house design system, and most of what we build is data-heavy: large tables, interactive charts, dashboards, and streaming, chat-driven experiences. Everything ships in containers to secure government environments. Responsibilities Own and evolve the shared frontend packages (app shell, component library, hooks, typed API client) that project teams build on, treating their public APIs as contracts with versioning and clear migration paths. Design and build reusable, config-driven components for data-heavy government applications: server-paginated tables, theme-aware charts, dashboards, forms, and chat and generative-UI surfaces driven by streaming events. Set the frontend testing strategy and build it out: component tests, integration tests against the real API, and end-to-end coverage for the flows that matter. Own frontend performance and bundle discipline: budgets, code splitting, render profiling, and keeping heavy dependencies (charting, grids, web components) from bloating every project app. Drive design-system direction: decide where Material UI ends and our in-house component library begins, and make that decision consistent across apps. Treat accessibility (Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 AA) and classification-aware UI (banners, markings) as first-class requirements. Partner with backend engineers on API shape, auth and session behavior, real-time event contracts, and the security posture of the browser surface (CSP, cookies, dependency hygiene). Support project teams adopting the platform: review their frontend code, unblock them, and pull recurring patterns back into the shared packages. Help plan and execute the migration of our existing product frontend onto the new platform without pausing feature delivery. Mentor engineers and raise the standard for frontend work across the company. Skills & Qualifications S in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience. 6+ years building production web applications with deep expertise in React and TypeScript. Experience owning a shared component library, design system, or frontend platform consumed by other teams, including package publishing, versioning, and breaking-change management. Strong grasp of modern React: hooks, Suspense, concurrent rendering, server-state libraries (TanStack Query or similar), and judgment about when client state (Zustand, Redux, or similar) is warranted. Fluency with the build and tooling layer: Vite, pnpm workspaces, ESLint, TypeScript project configuration, and CI for frontend packages. Experience shipping frontend tests that catch real regressions (Vitest or Jest with Testing Library, Playwright or Cypress). Experience building data-dense UIs: large tables with server-side pagination, interactive charts, dashboards. Working knowledge of browser security: session cookies, CSP, XSS, CSRF, and dependency supply chain. Clear written communication. Much of this role is design docs, code review, and documentation that other teams rely on. Nice to Have Experience with Web Components / Lit and integrating them into React. Experience with Material UI theming at scale, or building a theming system shared across multiple applications. Experience with streaming UIs (Server-Sent Events, WebSockets) or generative / LLM-driven interfaces. Experience with data visualization libraries (Plotly, D3, ECharts) and graph or flow editors (React Flow). Experience shipping software into DoD or other regulated environments (Platform One, GovCloud, air-gapped networks), and familiarity with Section 508 audits. Knowledge of NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, and CMMC 2.0 as they affect frontend and browser security. Experience migrating a legacy frontend onto a new platform while the product keeps shipping. Startup experience on a growing team, and a desire to mentor more junior engineers. What we offer you At Virtualitics , you’ll join a high-performance team of scientists, strategists, and servicemembers building AI that operates in the world’s most demanding environments. The problems we solve matter — and so does the opportunity to grow while solving them. You’ll have meaningful ownership from day one, with the ability to accelerate your career alongside a company scaling rapidly in national security and critical infrastructure. We offer highly competitive compensation, meaningful equity participation, and fully paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents. Our benefits also include unlimited PTO and flexible work arrangements, with remote flexibility and hybrid options for team members based in the Los Angeles or Washington, DC areas. Description: Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Design and implement UX workflows for clinical study management, data analytics, and patient diagnostics. Own the user experience, performance, reliability, and observability of the web apps and features you develop, leveraging feedback from real users in a diverse set of use cases and environments. Partner with product designers and cross-functional teams to develop user-centric capabilities that empower a wide set of user personas, both internally and externally. You're adept at identifying optimization bottlenecks, and debuggers and code profiling tools are an important part of your toolkit. Strong communication skills and comfort working in a collaborative, async environment. Bonus points if you've: Worked on applications for clinical trials, patients, or in some other regulated environment. Have experience in EEG or with DSP. Have worked on back-end systems or infrastructure. Contributed to open source React/Typescript projects. The salary range for this role is $170,000 – $190,000. This role focuses on the frontend applications and shared tooling that power those experiences. We're hiring a Senior Frontend Engineer who works AI-first: someone who treats AI as a core part of how they build software and break down ambiguous problems. That includes building workflows, reviewing their work critically, and course-correcting when things go sideways. You'll help build good habits for people and agents to work together, and use that to ship real features faster, alongside plenty of hands-on engineering of your own. Establish and maintain shared internal SDKs, component libraries, and boilerplate used across frontend teams. Set up agent-assisted workflows to ship faster, and review everything before it merges. Strong system design instincts: tradeoffs, edge cases, and performance budgets, in the browser and the pipeline. Daily use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent), with the judgment to critically review AI-generated code and own what gets merged. Clear, empathetic communicator: scopes ambiguous work, flags spec gaps, and disagrees constructively across teams. Nice to Haves Comfortable across the full delivery pipeline: build tooling, CI/CD (GitLab CI), and containerized deployments (Docker). Cloud infrastructure ownership Shared component/design system or boilerplate experience Publishing/versioning internal npm packages Observability/monitoring tooling in a frontend context B2B or point-of-sale experience in the attractions/venue industry AI Literacy We expect Senior Frontend Engineers to be genuinely fluent with AI-assisted development, not just occasional users of autocomplete. Comfort building the guardrails that keep agentic work reliable: repo conventions, scoped rules, and quality gates for non-trivial changes. Careful review of AI-generated diffs, catching plausible-but-wrong logic and security issues around payments and PII, and owning whatever you merge. Description: what to expect WHAT WE DO We are a startup digital agency, and no two projects, clients, or even days look the same. In ecommerce we build on Shopify and Liquid and Next.js, with custom AWS microservices and apps that take Shopify well past the defaults. On the marketing side we build highly customised sites in Next.js and React, with careful design and animation and a real focus on how the page performs and feels. In automotive we build full platforms, from stock-car locators to configurators and more. Across all of it, we bring AI into the work through our own products. Here nothing will be fixed. You will work across changing projects and settings, on long builds that run for months and shorter spikes to figure out how a business can actually use AI, and you will help us rethink how agency work is done. Sound like your kind of place? Here is what we need from you. your competencies YOUR PROFILE Mindset Is your goal to deliver great software, whether the problem is easy or hard? Do you push deeper than most to find the right solution, not just the first one that works? Then you are the person we need. Responsibility You own what you build, all the way through, not just until it ships and becomes someone else's problem. The parts that go smoothly and the parts that get messy are both yours to see through. You bring your ideas, experience and your curiosity, you use AI to build better and faster, and you stand behind what you put your name on. Drive By now the drive is a track record, not a promise. You have years of hard problems behind you and it shows. You understand the whole stack, or you close any gap in it fast, and the hard problems are the ones you go looking for. You are the one who takes the piece nobody else can crack and finds a way through, then leaves the ground solid enough for everyone else to build on. If the hardest part of a project is not the part you reach for, this is not your seat. What you bring to the table: You work across crafts, not in a corner. You are close with developers, designers, and strategists, and you would rather build in the open than behind a wall. You make the team better. You speak up when something can be sharper, and you share what you learn instead of sitting on it. You care whether the client wins. You focus on the quality of the product and the experience, not just the ticket in front of you. what you can look forward to What you will actually do: We build complex, end-to-end products for both big-name and niche clients. You are the strongest technical hands on the team, the one the hardest problems land on. Day to day, that means: Taking the hardest parts of the build and shipping them, the pieces others get stuck on. Laying the foundations: the architecture, the patterns, and the setup that let the rest of the team move fast and safely. Jumping in where something turned out harder than planned and getting it unstuck. Supporting the team on architecture calls and the technical side of client conversations. You’re enjoying being part of a team, not a remote desk which prefers to work in isolation most of the time. The tech stack you will work with: Languages and frameworks: React, Next.js, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Python. A new language should not slow you down for long. APIs: REST and GraphQL, Auth (SSO, SAML, OIDC) Cloud: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform Delivery: Creation and maintenance of CI/CD AI tooling: Claude, Cursor, Pi, Antigravity, plus your and our own Skills and MCP setup Who you will work with We are a bunch of colleagues originally from similar backgrounds who got tired of how things were usually done and set out to find better ways. That is the whole reason this company exists, and it is still what we are doing. We are not a place of rockstars and egos. People here ask questions out loud, show rough work without flinching, and would rather help each other get something right than look clever alone. We push each other, in the good way, and we do not take ourselves too seriously while we are at it. You would be joining that. You’ll work closely with the crafts, designers and strategists, and just as easily with the people steering the projects and the business. There is no wall between you and any of it. Take on the parts you are ready for, and when you want more, a pitch, a client conversation, a bigger call, speak up at the right moment and the door is open. Smaller team. More ownership. Bigger work. Originally posted on Himalayas

Learn and apply the team's existing patterns for authentication, authorization, and service-layer design as you contribute to new features. Bring a thoughtful approach to AI-assisted development: know when suggestions are good, when they need revision, and when to discard them entirely. Experiment with AI tooling beyond basic code completion, such as using agents or custom skills to automate repetitive development tasks, generate test scaffolding, or accelerate documentation. Share what you learn about effective AI tooling with your team, contributing to a culture where the team improves its use of these tools over time. What We're Looking For Required 3 to 4 years of professional software engineering experience in a full-stack or backend-leaning role. Solid hands-on experience with Vue 3 using the Composition API; you have built real features with it, not just followed tutorials. Hands-on experience with Java and Spring Boot, building and maintaining REST APIs in a production environment. Working knowledge of relational databases: writing queries, understanding joins and indexes, and contributing to schema design. Familiarity with TypeScript in a frontend codebase; comfortable with types, interfaces, and generics at a working level. Experience writing tests across the stack: Vitest for Vue 3 component and unit testing on the frontend, JUnit for unit and integration testing on the backend. Experience with Pinia for state management in Vue 3 applications. Familiarity with Git workflows in a team environment: branching, pull requests, code review, and resolving conflicts. Awareness and hands-on experimentation with AI coding tools; you have used them in your own workflow and formed a view on where they help. Clear communication: able to ask good questions, articulate what you are working on, and flag blockers early rather than late. Nice to Have Experience working on enterprise software, particularly in finance, ERP, or performance management domains. Exposure to custom AI agents or workflow automation tools beyond basic code completion. Experience with CI/CD pipelines and containerised environments (Docker, GitHub Actions). Knowledge of Spring Security or similar frameworks for authentication and authorization. Experience with agile delivery practices including sprint planning, estimation, and retrospectives. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Who Thrives in This Role The right person for this role is comfortable on both sides of the stack and does not wait to be told exactly what to do. They take ownership of a piece of work, figure out what they need to know, and see it through. They are not the loudest person in the room, but they contribute meaningfully in design discussions and code reviews, and their teammates notice when they are not around. Description: JTX is our trading app, and it runs on the fastest market infrastructure on Solana, which we also built. What nobody has done yet is make that speed something a trader can feel. That is this job. JTX is live. Two frontend engineers built it to this point and you would be the third. The work now is one to a hundred: harden what exists, make it hold up under real volume, expand onto mobile, and raise the ceiling on every screen a trader touches. We're a small team with product-market fit. That means: High ownership: every team member drives significant technical decisions and shapes our product roadmap. Fast execution: we ship rapidly and iterate based on real-world feedback. Progress, not motion. High quality bar: the details are the product. We don't trade them for speed. About the Position You'll own the surface of JTX across web and mobile: order entry, market data, charts, positions, execution quality, onboarding, and the wallet flows underneath all of it. The role suits a generalist with strong taste. You'll partner with design, product, and the infrastructure team, and you'll make architectural calls that stick for years. If you've spent time thinking about how markets actually work on Solana and want to build the product layer on top of that, this is the role. Stack: React 19 + TypeScript on Next.js. Jotai + TanStack Query. Tailwind with a token-based design system. TradingView Advanced Charts on our own datafeed. Privy wallets. WebSockets to our engine. Web ships as a PWA; native mobile apps are in development. What's Hard Right Now Data freshness: several live WebSocket streams (order book, trades, candles, stats) feed many panels at once; keeping them fast, consistent with each other, and honest through async gaps (stale quotes, pending fills) Performance: a data-dense terminal that stays smooth under constant streaming updates, including on mid-range hardware Security: wallet signing, session auth, strict CSP, hardened supply chain Shipping volume: three engineers own the entire surface of a live exchange; the backlog is bigger than the team, so throughput and prioritization are part of the job Keeping product behavior and design language consistent between web and mobile while being very attentive to nuances of each mobile platform Making execution quality something a trader can see in a glance instead of something they take on faith What You'll Do Build and own the JTX client across web and mobile Ship real-time trading interfaces: order books, charts, order entry, positions, fill and execution visibility Hit tight latency and render budgets against streaming market data, and decide what belongs on the client versus the server Build wallet and signing flows, including self-custodial and embedded wallet onboarding Own the shared component, state, and data layers the rest of the product team builds on Make architectural decisions that hold as the codebase, the team, and the user base grow by an order of magnitude Ship fast, watch real users, iterate What We're Looking For Attention to detail bordering on obsessive. You can look at a screen and say what is wrong with it, and it bothers you until it's fixed. 5+ years building production frontend, including something real-time, data dense, or financial Deep React and TypeScript. You can explain why a component re-rendered and then fix it. You write code, review designs, and hold the highest standards. Engineers respect a lead who understands the work, not one who manages it from a distance You build strength across the team. You know when to be hands-on and when to step back. You lead with depth and raise the others up, rather than being the single point of failure You own it. You take responsibility for the team's delivery, quality, and production reliability — not just your own output. When something breaks, you lead the investigation and fix You develop people. You invest time in mentoring and growing the team, and you can point to engineers who are better for having worked with you You're direct and honest. You give specific, timely feedback, and you hold a quality line without becoming a bottleneck You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially during incidents and in stakeholder updates — is essential You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation What You Get Real problems —trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. Balance is how we stay sharp Growth — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work. We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable. Description: Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call. Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to build the platform that catches data problems before they become business problems. About Us Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing. Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo. The Role You'll lead frontend work in one of our product teams: a TypeScript/Angular application with Storybook-driven components and Cypress e2e coverage, in front of a Java backend. You own the user experience end-to-end, from component architecture and state management down to the API shape, because the backend is yours to touch too. We're product engineers, not ticket-takers: you'll talk to users, shape the design with your PM, and ship without waiting for hand-offs. Frontend is your craft; full-stack is your reach. You'll spend most of your time in the frontend, and you can ship a backend endpoint when the feature needs it rather than filing a ticket and waiting. We also build agentically: AI coding agents are part of the daily workflow here, not an experiment on the side. What You'll Do Own complex, data-dense UIs: dashboards, monitoring views, large tables, diffs and drill-downs that stay fast and legible. Drive component architecture, state management, and frontend performance. Build with a component library and Storybook; keep the design system coherent as the product grows. Write tests at every layer. You'll help keep our Cypress e2e suite meaningful. Build the frontend of agentic features: interfaces where users direct, review, and act on LLM-powered workflows. Improve our systems for agentic development on the frontend: conventions, Storybook coverage, and tests that agents can build against reliably. Shape the APIs you consume, and implement backend changes (Java) when your feature needs them. Mentor backend-focused engineers on frontend, helping the team grow more full-stack and deliver features end to end. Work directly with product, design, and customers to decide what to build. Your opinion matters here. Hiring Process CV screen 20-minute phone screen First technical interview (45 min) Second technical interview (60 min) Culture fit (45 min) We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly. Requirements 5+ years building frontend for real products : complex single-page applications with real users, not just marketing sites. Expert TypeScript and deep experience with a modern framework: Angular preferred (it's what powers Soda Cloud); strong React/Vue engineers willing to work in Angular are welcome. Frontend craft : component architecture, state management, rendering performance, responsive design, and an eye for detail (you can spot a misaligned pixel). Testing as a habit : you actually write tests, including e2e (Cypress/Playwright). Working backend skills : you can read and modify a Java service, design an API from the consumer's perspective, and write competent SQL. Systems insight : you understand how an API's shape drives round-trips, data flow, and perceived latency in the UI. Agentic engineering : you ship production code with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) in the loop, and you know how to direct them well while keeping the quality bar high. Independence : you don't need hand-holding in a distributed, async team across 12+ countries. Fluent English. Good to Have Data-heavy or developer-tool products: data visualization, monitoring, analytics UIs. Design-system or component-library ownership. Multi-tenant SaaS at scale; high-growth startup experience. Python: our data engineering stack runs on it. Experience building agentic workflows into the product: LLM-powered features, tool-using agents, or AI-driven automation shipped to real users. Data quality, data management, data observability, or ML monitoring industry experience. Benefits What We Offer Compensation €85,000-120,000/year + equity. Fully remote (EU-based), with a Belgian office available if you want one. All the tokens you need, across all frontier models. Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement. A team of senior engineers who ship, across 12+ countries. Our Values We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions. ❤️ Why you will love to join Soda Be part of a transformation : data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it. Ownership from day one : if you see a bottleneck, you remove it. International culture : colleagues in 12+ countries. Work on your own terms : fully remote, flexible hours. 😡 What you might not love Rapidly changing priorities : our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done. Flexibility required : you will have to learn new things all the time. Originally posted on Himalayas

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters. What You'll Work On Complex full-stack features in TypeScript and Rust — from trader-facing interfaces to the application services behind them Real-time market-data presentation and high-throughput, low-latency application code across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency React and reactive state management (RX, MobX, or similar) for demanding, data-dense trading interfaces Distributed systems and real-time data over REST, WebSockets, and network protocols Architecture and solution design for the hardest technical problems the team faces Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make frontend behaviour visible Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional What We Need Technical: Strong full-stack engineering ability with deep TypeScript / JavaScript (ES6+) (5+ years) Solid experience with React and reactive state management (RX, MobX, or similar) Working knowledge of Rust , or the clear appetite and ability to get there — it's part of our stack Strong grasp of distributed systems, API design, and real-time data (REST, WebSockets, network protocols such as TCP/UDP and binary protocols) Comfortable reasoning about architecture and making defensible technical trade-offs Python for scripting, automation, and tooling is a bonus Git and Linux fundamentals Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential How you work: You ship. You're not just strong in the familiar parts of the stack — you pick up the unfamiliar and hold your own on the hardest work You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop You raise the bar. You review peers' work thoughtfully, mentor the engineers around you through the craft, and set a standard others calibrate to You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist You communicate. Description: About Us At Prenuvo , we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience across our domestic and global clinics, have allowed us to lead the change against “we caught it too late again". We're looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer I to join our eCommerce team, building the online booking experience patients use to choose a scan, find a clinic, pay, and schedule their appointment. You'll lead complex features in a Next.js and TypeScript application that serves customers in multiple countries, on flows where every screen directly affects conversion, revenue, and patient trust: product selection, checkout and payments, appointment scheduling across timezones, and our sales-assisted and partner booking paths. This is a high-impact role for someone who cares about the craft of the UI and about whether it actually works in production for every customer. If you enjoy solving ambiguous problems and owning outcomes rather than tickets, we'd love to hear from you. This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future). Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives! What You’ll Do Own features and components within an area of the booking experience, such as checkout and payments, scheduling, or the sales-assisted and partner flows, growing toward owning the area end to end. Work with Product and Marketing on growth: ship experiments on the booking funnel, then read the results honestly, including sample size, guardrail metrics, and whether a change is a real win or just noise. Build fast, accessible, customer-facing features with React, Next.js (App Router), and TypeScript. Contribute to frontend architecture and design, writing proposals you review with senior engineers: sensible server and client component boundaries, server state with TanStack Query, client state with Zustand, and type-safe forms with React Hook Form and Zod. Integrate the booking experience with our commerce APIs and third-party services, including Stripe, Affirm, commercetools, Voucherify, Salesforce, Auth0, and Google Maps. Instrument what you ship: Datadog RUM for errors and performance, PostHog for product analytics, feature flags, and experiments, and Google Tag Manager for marketing measurement, all respecting each customer's consent choices. Improve Core Web Vitals, bundle size, and rendering performance on a high-traffic, revenue-critical funnel. Make accessibility a default: semantic markup, keyboard and screen reader support, and automated accessibility checks in CI. Write automated tests at the right level: Vitest and Testing Library for components, MSW for API mocking, and Playwright for end-to-end booking flows. Own outcomes in production: ship behind feature flags, watch the dashboards after release, and follow through when something breaks. You are accountable for whether a feature works for customers, not just whether it merged. Partner closely with Product, Design, Marketing, and Backend engineers, contributing to our shared component library and agreeing the API contracts the frontend depends on. Provide technical guidance through design discussions and high-quality code review, and mentor junior engineers. Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully as part of a structured build, review, and test workflow. What You’ll Bring Typically 4+ years of professional frontend engineering experience, including at least 3 years building production applications with React and TypeScript. Strong experience with Next.js or a comparable React framework, including server-side rendering, routing, and the tradeoffs between server and client rendering. Deep understanding of browser fundamentals: semantic HTML, modern CSS and responsive layout, the event loop, network and caching behavior, and the rendering pipeline. Experience with modern data-fetching and state management patterns (TanStack Query, Zustand, Redux, or similar) and with complex, validated, multi-step forms. Strong testing practices across unit, component, and end-to-end layers, using tools such as Vitest or Jest, Testing Library, and Playwright or Cypress. Experience building checkout, payment, or other transactional flows where correctness and reliability matter. Working knowledge of web accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) and web performance (Core Web Vitals). Experience with frontend observability and product analytics tools such as Datadog RUM, Sentry, PostHog, or Google Analytics. Hands-on experience with modern CI/CD practices and cloud hosting (for example GitHub Actions and AWS). A track record of leading complex features from design through production. A startup mindset: comfortable taking on ambiguous work, knowing when to pull in a second opinion on an approach, and able to balance speed with quality. Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across engineering, design, and business teams. Nice to Have Experience with Stripe.js and payment method integrations, including buy now, pay later providers such as Affirm. Experience with headless commerce platforms such as commercetools, or promotion engines such as Voucherify. Experience with Tailwind CSS and building on top of a design system or component library. Experience with consent management platforms (such as OneTrust), Google Tag Manager, and privacy-aware analytics. Experience with multi-region products: multiple currencies and locales, and correct date, time, and timezone handling. Growth engineering experience: working on a team that owns acquisition, activation, or conversion metrics, and shipping many small experiments quickly. Experience with funnel analytics and marketing attribution: event tracking plans, UTM and referral attribution, and conversion tracking into ad platforms such as Google Ads and Meta. Experience building growth surfaces such as landing pages, email capture, referral programs, promo codes, and abandoned-cart recovery. Experience with authentication and identity providers such as Auth0. Experience with scheduling, booking, or consumer healthcare applications, or working in highly regulated industries. Description: Senior Software Engineer, Front End – Dashboard About Caliza Caliza is commercial banking infrastructure for companies that operate across borders. Most global businesses still piece together several banks, FX providers and spreadsheets to move money. Caliza replaces that with one platform and API: hold USD accounts, collect and pay in 33+ currencies, and convert between fiat and stablecoins, over local rails, SWIFT or stablecoins, in minutes instead of days. On top of that, we’re building the treasury layer: programmable accounts, approval policies, automated reconciliation and working capital, run by a customer’s finance team or their AI agents. Our customers are importers, exporters, FX brokers, payment companies and fintechs across the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia. We’re licensed and regulated across our core markets, and our team has built financial infrastructure at Visa, Nubank, EBANX, Flutterwave, Upstart, Intuit and Silicon Valley Bank. Our backers Initialized Capital, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Abstract Ventures, New Form Capital, QED Investors, Valor Capital and Quona Capital, along with the founders of Flutterwave, Chipper Cash, Rappi, Pomelo, Dock, Remesa Online and Anchorage. About the role The Caliza dashboard is where our customers see and control money moving across rails, currencies and countries. When a payment is in flight, a balance changes, or a compliance check is pending, the dashboard has to show it accurately and immediately, even across thousands of transactions. As a Senior Software Engineer focused on the dashboard, you'll own features end to end, including transaction and settlement views, balances across currencies, search and filtering, exports and reporting, and the permissions that control who sees and does what. You'll work closely with design, product, back-end and compliance. Location: Remote, open to candidates based in Latin America. Professional English required. In your first six months, you'll Design and build the real-time dashboard experience, so customers see payment and balance changes as they happen. Make large transaction tables fast and usable, with solid filtering, search and export. Improve how we show payment and settlement state, so users always know where money is and what happens next. Strengthen our shared component library and set front-end conventions for testing, performance and accessibility. What you'll be doing Build and maintain the dashboard in TypeScript and React. Design data-dense interfaces: tables, detail views, charts and reports. Integrate with back-end APIs, handling the loading, error and edge-case states that matter when money is involved. Contribute to our back-end services in Kotlin and Spring Boot when a feature needs it, such as adding or changing the APIs the dashboard depends on. Implement role-based access so each user sees exactly what they should. Own performance, from rendering large data sets to efficient data fetching. Write meaningful automated tests and review your teammates' code. Work with product and design from early concept through launch. What we're looking for 5+ years of professional front-end development experience. Deep expertise in TypeScript and React. Experience with data fetching, caching and state management tools such as Redux Toolkit and TanStack Query. Experience building real-time interfaces (websockets, live updates). Comfort working across the stack: you're happy to make back-end changes when a feature needs them. Experience building data-heavy applications such as dashboards, admin tools or analytics products. Strong product sense: you care about building rich, highly usable interfaces, not just shipping tickets. A strong grasp of front-end security: handling sensitive data, XSS/CSRF protection, and secure authentication flows. Real experience writing automated tests and caring about test quality. Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development in your daily work, with the judgment to review and question what the tools produce. Solid understanding of performance and accessibility (WCAG). Comfort with high autonomy and ambiguity in a fast-moving, remote startup. Clear written communication. Most of our collaboration is async. Nice to have Experience in fintech, payments, banking or crypto products. Back-end experience with Kotlin or Java and Spring Boot. Experience building or maintaining a design system. Experience with multiple currencies, languages, and number and date formats. How we work We use AI coding tools every day and expect you to as well. They make us faster at the routine parts of the work. But you own every line you ship: you understand it, test it, and can defend it in review. Because we handle financial data, we follow clear rules about what code and data can go into which tools. Description: As an engineer at Bask you will work directly with the CEO and CTO to build and design the software infrastructure that will serve as the backbone of telehealth. We are looking to expand our software engineers, seeking those with deep rooted entrepreneurial spirit. Our serverless platform is a multi-tenant monorepo — Next.js and React on the front, tRPC and Prisma behind it, deployed on SST, TypeScript throughout. One engineer can follow a change from a form field to the database without crossing a team boundary. That's the point. Engineering at Bask Health is AI-first and builder-led. Work starts with general understanding of problem, moves to tools like Claude and Cursor for further investigation, making a plan and building, tested on staging with realistic data, released to production, tested with real patient and care teams, and then back for systems and polish. AI is a default part of how we work, not a side experiment — because moving fast in healthcare requires every advantage. We are looking for engineers who take end-to-end ownership, treat AI as a real collaborator, and care deeply about building software that meaningfully improves how healthcare is delivered. What You'll Do Design, build, and ship high-quality product experiences. Own key surfaces end to end, from concept through production. Write elegant, well-tested code — we have a real test suite and we intend to keep it that way. Work across the stack. Follow a feature from the interface through the API to the database. No handoffs, no waiting on another team. Work AI-first with Cursor and Claude Code. Use LLMs as your starting point. Draft intent, explore implementations, scaffold components, and refactor with AI in the loop. Apply your own judgment to meet the quality bar healthcare demands. Prototype fast and validate with real users. Build and test quickly with real patients and care teams. Use what you learn to refine before fully committing — especially in sensitive clinical contexts where getting it right matters. Build for scale and own the codebase. Translate product needs into reusable, well-architected patterns that make the next feature faster to ship. Make automation legible and trustworthy. Build systems that clearly communicate what AI and automation are doing on behalf of patients and providers. Earn trust through transparency, reliability, and thoughtful defaults. Champion performance, accessibility, and reliability. Ship work that is fast, robust, and accessible. Partner across the team to debug, optimize, and raise the bar over time. Share AI-native workflows. Document prompts, patterns, and workflows that work, so we move faster together without cutting corners that matter to patient outcomes. We are a highly collaborative team. Requirements A full-stack generalist who has taken a product from 0 to 1 and can apply that instinct inside a system that already has real patients on it. Entrepreneurial, willing to roll up their sleeves, and drawn to a mission that disrupts how healthcare gets delivered. 5+ Years of experience You are dangerous on the frontend of the stack. You are a highly skilled dev (React, TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind and JavaScript). You also have backend skills (tRPC, Drizzle ORM, SQL, Node, SST). You can work independently and are comfortable owning entire projects or large areas of the codebase. Strong experience building paid products and services is preferred. React Native or Expo experience is a plus. You are a strong communicator, able to clearly articulate technical problems, constraints, and timelines. You are comfortable working in a fast-paced, unstructured, startup environment. Originally posted on Himalayas

We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations. Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things. Role As a Backend Engineer, AI, you own the inference and orchestration layer that powers every AI interaction in the product. Your work sits between models and users, where latency, correctness, reliability, and cost directly impact real-world experience. You will build and operate production systems that turn model capability into fast, stable, observable APIs used across mobile and desktop clients. Focus Build and operate backend systems that serve AI-powered features in production. Design inference pipelines, orchestration layers, and service boundaries around models. Own production concerns: monitoring, logging, alerting, and incident response. Optimize latency and throughput across inference, caching, batching, and streaming. Ideal Experiences Strong backend engineering fundamentals in production environments. Experience running high-throughput, low-latency services. Familiarity with AI inference patterns (LLMs, embeddings, multimodal). Comfortable debugging distributed systems under load. Bias toward shipping and learning from production behavior. Outcomes Backend systems run reliably at scale, handling production AI traffic with low latency and high throughput. APIs are stable, clear, and support seamless integration with frontend and ML systems. Production incidents are quickly detected, diagnosed, and resolved, minimizing user impact. Iterative improvements based on real usage continuously increase system performance and reliability. Tech Stack Python NodeJs Pytorch OpenAI / Anthropic / open-source LLMs SQl & noSQL Kubernetes Docker How We Work The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product Interview process If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews. Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite. We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally. Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: At Midas , we tackle real-world engineering challenges to reshape the future of finance. Our mission is to build the fastest and most reliable products, delivering a seamless experience that empowers everyone to manage their money effortlessly. More than 3.5 million users use our product. Backed by an $80M Series B , the largest fintech investment ever in Turkey, we are scaling faster than ever. Read Before You Apply 🚨 This role is not for everyone. We are looking for outlier engineers who: Have owned products end-to-end , from idea to production monitoring. Have managed live incidents , written post-mortems, and implemented long-term fixes. Passionate about delivering exceptional product experiences and maximizing user impact , beyond just writing code. Years of experience don’t matter — what matters is the depth of ownership, incident handling, and product impact you’ve delivered. If this doesn’t sound like you, no worries — Midas has other opportunities that may be a better fit. What You’ll Do Build high performance, low latency, scalable web application for real-time trading and financial data. Investigate and solve complex engineering problems across the frontend, APIs, and real-time data flows. Contribute to technical decisions and continuously improve the performance, reliability, and maintainability of the platform. Collaborate closely with product, design, backend, and other engineering teams to build and evolve Atlas. What We’re Looking For Strong fundamentals and a solid understanding of the challenges involved in building reliable, performant web applications. Good problem solving and debugging skills, with a willingness to dig into unfamiliar or complex problems. A willingness to take ownership, learn quickly, and grow with the product and the team. An interest in how engineering decisions affect performance, reliability, and user experience. Strong communication and collaboration skills. Nice to have Up to 5 years of professional software engineering experience. Experience building applications with React, Next.js, Redux, REST or GraphQL. Experience with real-time systems and high frequency data updates using technologies such as WebSockets or SSE. Familiarity with financial systems, trading platforms, or market data. Experience with browser performance profiling and optimization. How We Work Full ownership — you don’t wait, you solve. First principles mindset — you question assumptions and rebuild where needed. Balance speed & quality — you ship fast, but always clean. Product mindset — you care about the user impact, not just the code. Calm under pressure — incidents happen; you lead with clarity and composure. We don’t measure success by how many features you ship — but by the impact your work has on millions of users . If you thrive in high-stakes environments, love solving real problems, and own your work end-to-end, we want to meet you. Originally posted on Himalayas
